Family Visa - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco.
Issued to members of an Algerian family who is registered at the Consulate General. Required: 1. visa application form completed on-screen, printed, dated, hand-signed; 2. one recent standard photo; 3. copy of the Algerian relative's consular card; 4. copy of proof of relationship (marriage or birth certificate); 5. original passport and copy of main photo page, valid at least six months with at least two blank pages; 6. for non-US passports, copy of US legal residency document (Green Card or appropriate visa); 7. proof of residence within the consulate's jurisdiction (driver's license, utility bill, bank or credit card statement, insurance policy or bill); 8. USPS Priority Mail return envelope (recommended).
Fee: 'The visa fee for US passports is 160$ (Non-refundable).' Other passports per a separate fee list (not retrieved). Payment by USPS money order.

title: Transit Visa - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
text:
Transit Visa - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco.
Issued to people transiting through the Algerian territory who hold an entry visa for their destination country. Maximum duration: 7 days. Required: application form completed on-screen, printed, dated, hand-signed; one recent standard photo; hotel reservation; copy of airline itinerary; most recent statement of financial resources or proof of income; original passport and copy of main photo page (valid at least 6 months, at least two blank pages); for non-US passports, copy of US legal residency document; proof of address within the consular jurisdiction; optional Priority Mail Express return envelope.
Fee: US passports $160 (non-refundable); other passports per separate list. Payment by USPS money order.

title: Regularization of the Situation of Algerian Citizens Residing Abroad - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
text:
Regularization announcement - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco.
The Consulate General informs Algerian nationals in its consular jurisdiction about exceptional measures, announced under a decision of President Abdelmadjid Tebboune, allowing Algerian citizens abroad in vulnerable or irregular situations who face judicial or administrative proceedings (notably young people facing proceedings for misdemeanors affecting public order) to regularize their legal status. To apply: contact the consular service, submit the approved form ('Regularization_Request_Form') and the required supporting documents. The Consulate will support applicants and track requests until a final decision is issued. No deadlines or fees stated.

title: Jurisdiction - Consular Coverage (Embassy of Algeria in Washington) - Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco
text:
Algerian consular jurisdiction in the United States (Embassy of Algeria in Washington page).
Consulate General of Algeria in San Francisco (19 states): California, Arizona, Nevada, Oregon, Washington, Utah, Colorado, Hawaii, Alaska, North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Oklahoma, Texas, Kansas, Wyoming, Montana, Idaho, New Mexico.
Consulate General of Algeria in New York (25 states): Alabama, Arkansas, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Vermont, Wisconsin.
Embassy of Algeria in Washington, D.C.: Delaware, Maryland, North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia, West Virginia, Washington D.C.
San Francisco consulate address (from its service pages): 465 California St., Suite 900, San Francisco, CA 94104. Email (passport status help): secretariat@cgalgeriasf.org.

title: Mobile Station to Chicago 2023 - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text: Announcement - Consulate General of Algeria in New York (cgnewyork.mfa.gov.dz). The Consulate General planned a mobile biometric station in Chicago in 2023 for photo and fingerprint taking for biometric passports, the only procedure requiring in-person appearance (applicants over 12). Registered nationals whose passports had expired or would be invalid by November 15, 2023 had to mail their files to the Consulate before May 8, 2023. Passport, registration renewal and first registration applications could be sent together. Fingerprinting in Chicago was only possible if the application had already been sent to the New York Consulate. 'NO OTHER SERVICE SUCH AS VISA, REGISTRATION, PROXY ETC.. WILL BE GRANTED.' Contact: ms@algeria-cgny.org. Hours stated on the site: all consular services except visas, Tuesday to Saturday 9 am to 3 pm (Saturday 9 am to 2:30 pm); visa lodging Tuesday to Friday 9 am to 12 pm. (Historical 2023 announcement.)

title: Biometric Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
Biometric Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in New York.
Biometric passports are issued to Algerian citizens living abroad permanently, after their consular registration is finalized. Start renewal about six months before the current passport expires. Passports are issued in Algeria, so there is usually a delay of several weeks. Track status with the number on your receipt about one week after fingerprint/photo/signature capture on the Algerian Ministry of the Interior passport tracking site. Passport services require an appointment; all other consular services are available without one.
Under 12: no fingerprinting or in-person pickup needed; send all documents by mail. 12 and older: must appear in person for fingerprinting; sending the application by mail before attending is recommended.
First-time: passport form completed and signed (by legal tutor for minors); two 2x2 inch (51x51 mm) recent photos, white background, neutral expression, no smile, clear forehead; original 12-S birth certificate; copy of proof of US residency (US passport, Green Card, US birth certificate, or appropriate visa); USPS Priority Mail return envelope.
Renewal: passport renewal form completed and signed (by legal tutor for minors); two 2x2 photos; original 12-S birth certificate only if the old biometric passport was not issued by the Consulate General in New York; copy of proof of US residency; USPS Priority Mail return envelope.
Book options: Standard (28 pages) or Large (48 pages). Fees by USPS money order. Standard fees per the official fee page: students and children under 19 - $37.50 (28 pages), $56.25 (48 pages); employed or unemployed - $75.00 (28 pages), $112.50 (48 pages). The passport page also lists 'passport and penalty fees' for lost, stolen, damaged or late renewal: $100, $118.75, $200, $237.50 (category mapping not explicit on the page; confirm with the consulate).

title: Emergency Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
Emergency Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in New York.
The emergency passport is a non-biometric, machine-readable passport printed at Algerian embassies and consulates and, in some cases, by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Algiers. Its validity is non-extendable and ranges from 3 months to one year depending on purpose.
A. Issued by the Consulate General: 1. written request to the Consul General explaining the need; 2. emergency passport application form, completed and signed; 3. proof of Algerian nationality (old passport, consular card, or identity card); 4. proof of address in the consulate's states of jurisdiction; 5. proof of the emergency (e.g. relative's death certificate, summons, immigration or marriage appointment); 6. two (2) current passport photos with plain white background; 7. USPS money order for $75 USD.
B. Issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (in Algeria): application form provided by the MFA, completed and signed; proof of foreign residence; consular registration card; statement from any police station in Algeria confirming loss, theft or deterioration; two current passport photos; receipt from Algerian tax services showing payment of 6,000 DA.
Contact: (917) 251-9795.

title: Travel Document (Laissez-passer) - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
Laissez-passer - Consulate General of Algeria in New York.
'The laissez-passer is a travel document issued to Algerian nationals not registered at the Consulate General' to return to Algeria when the passport is lost, stolen or expired; also issued to newborns in the USA whose Algerian parents are visiting as tourists or lack legal immigration status. Valid up to 30 days, one-way to Algeria by the shortest route. 'The laissez-passer request must be submitted to our services at the latest, 72 hours before the departure date.'
All applicants: application form filled out and signed; two recent photographs; flight ticket; self-addressed return envelope if mailed back.
Adults: proof of Algerian nationality (passport, national identity card, or military card with photo); the damaged Algerian passport, if applicable; signed statement from a Police Department on damage, loss or theft.
Newborns/minors: proof of father's or mother's Algerian nationality; original full-version birth certificate of the child; if the father is Algerian and not present, his authorization (notarized if mailed, or legalized by an administrative officer (Commune) in Algeria if he is there).
Civil status documents (birth/marriage certificates, family book), driving licenses and foreign documents are not accepted as proof of nationality. No fee stated on this page.

title: Biometric National Identity Card - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
Biometric National Identity Card (CNIBE) - Consulate General of Algeria in New York.
Issued to Algerian citizens permanently residing abroad after consular registration. Applicants of any age may apply online after obtaining a biometric passport (holders with a National Identification Number (NIN) can use passeport.interieur.gov.dz). Children under 12 are exempt from fingerprinting; their presence is not required for filing or collection. Applicants 12 and older must attend fingerprinting in person; no appointment needed, but sending the application before attending is recommended.
First-time (19+): ID form completed and signed; two recent 2x2 inch (51x51 mm) photos, white background, neutral expression, no smile, clear forehead; original 12-S birth certificate; USPS Priority Mail return envelope. Under 19: same, form signed by the legal tutor.
Renewal: ID renewal form completed and signed (by legal tutor for minors); two photos; original 12-S birth certificate; USPS Priority Mail return envelope. Option 1: online application; option 2 (if online does not work): submit the renewal documents.
Fees (official fee page): old ID in possession - free; old ID damaged or lost - $15.00 penalty, USPS money order. No processing time stated.

title: Consular Registration - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
Consular Registration - Consulate General of Algeria in New York.
Algerian citizens living permanently overseas must complete consular registration before obtaining passports or registering to vote. A consular card is issued free of charge, valid for 5 years. Submit in person without appointment or by mail to 15 East 47th Street, New York, NY 10017.
Cannot apply if you: 1. entered the US temporarily for business (B1), tourism (B2), or both (B1/B2); 2. hold a work permit not valid for re-entry; 3. are considered an undocumented immigrant. Under 19: only the parent's (or legal guardian's) registration is needed; no consular card until age 19.
Request types: first-time; renewal; transfer from another embassy/consulate (registration granted once the file is received from the previous post).
All requests: application form (Registration_form.pdf) completed and signed; two recent 2x2 inch (51x51 mm) photos; self-addressed stamped envelope.
First-time (varies by status - US-born citizen, naturalized, permanent resident, visa holder A/F/G/H/J): original full-size birth certificate (E.C 12 Copie integrale if born in Algeria; any birth certificate if born abroad; US birth certificate for US-born); one parent's birth certificate or Algerian nationality certificate (not needed if parent holds a consular card); if born overseas, certificate of Algerian nationality or birth certificates of two male ascendants born in Algeria; copy of front and back of green card (permanent residents; initial green card for naturalized); copy of US passport or naturalization certificate (citizens); copy of nonimmigrant visa and/or USCIS document (visa holders); copy of US entry visa; copy of Algerian passport photo page if available; proof of employment, self-employment or school enrollment.
Renewal: expired consular card (if available); copy of US passport / naturalization certificate / green card / visa document (if different from initial registration); proof of employment or enrollment (if different); photos; stamped envelope.
Transfer of file: same as first-time minus the parent documents.

title: Civil Status - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
Civil Status Services - Consulate General of Algeria in New York.
No appointment needed; file in person or by mail. Mailed applications must include a USPS Priority Mail return envelope; incomplete mailed applications are returned.
Birth: Algerian parent(s) must report a newborn's birth. The 12-S (extract of birth certificate) is required for a biometric passport or ID card. Born in Algeria: obtain the 12-S online through the Ministry of the Interior website, or at the Town Hall of the birth place in person or through a power of attorney issued by the consulate. Born in the US: Birth Report form completed and signed; original or certified copy of the full birth certificate from city hall including time of birth (returned after verification); copy of proof of Algerian nationality and identity (passport, national ID, consular card, or military card; for minors a parent's); family book if available. Born in another country: same, with the birth certificate from that country. Parents' names must match the Algerian civil status register.
Marriage: a marriage of an Algerian national in the US must be registered; a family book (livret de famille) is issued after registration, free of charge. Documents: Marriage Registration descriptive form completed and signed; original US marriage certificate (returned after verification); copy of proof of Algerian nationality; original birth certificates of both spouses (the Algerian national's issued within the last three months).
Divorce: a US or other foreign divorce has no effect in Algeria unless recognized by an Algerian court ('Exequatur'), carried out in Algeria, optionally through a lawyer.
Death / repatriation of remains: the consulate assists families; funeral services handle transfer paperwork; the consulate transcribes the death, issues an Algerian death certificate and the 'Autorisation de Transfert de corps'. Repatriation documents: 1. death report completed and signed; 2. birth certificate of the deceased; 3. medical letter from the Department of Health stating the death was not from an infectious or communicable disease; 4. original US death certificate; 5. embalming certificate; 6. transit permit from City Hall; 7. certificate that the body was prepared according to Muslim rituals; 8. copy of the deceased's proof of Algerian nationality; 9. airway bill; 10. family book if available. Death registration only: items 1, 2, 4, 8, 10. Names must match the civil status register.
Correction of errors (birth, marriage, death certificates): application form; original certificate from the place of the event (foreign-language documents translated into Arabic); copy of the certificate with the error; supporting identity documents (birth errors), spouses' birth certificates with annotations (marriage errors), or the deceased's birth and marriage certificates and the applicant's birth certificate and proof of relationship (death errors). Submission does not rule out a judicial investigation.
Fees (official fee page): 12-S birth certificate free; duplicate of family book $25.00; translation of family record book $25.00.

title: Criminal Record - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
Criminal Record (Casier Judiciaire No. 3) - Consulate General of Algeria in New York.
Registered members of the Algerian community in the consulate's jurisdiction can request a copy of their criminal record (Bulletin No. 3) through the consulate; requests can also be made directly to the relevant services under a ministerial instruction of June 24, 2010 by the Ministers of Foreign Affairs and Justice.
Algerian citizens abroad: application form (PDF); birth certificate; copy of consular card; pre-paid self-addressed return envelope.
Non-Algerians who resided in Algeria: application form; valid ID; proof of residency in Algeria; pre-paid self-addressed return envelope.
Fee: free (per the official fee page). No appointment needed. Note: the page text refers to '44 states' of jurisdiction, which predates the San Francisco consulate; current NY jurisdiction is 25 states.

title: Nationality Certificate - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
Algerian Nationality Certificate - Consulate General of Algeria in New York.
Issued to Algerian nationals established within the consular jurisdiction, under Articles 6 and 7 of the Nationality Law (Order No. 70-86 of 15 December 1970, amended by Order No. 05-01 of 27 February 2005). The Consulate submits the application through the Ministry of Justice platform; after processing by the competent judicial authorities the certificate is delivered electronically, signed. No appointment needed; apply in person or by mail (mail: notarized copies and a USPS Priority Mail return envelope).
Identity proof (one): state ID, driver license, US passport or passport card, US military card, military dependent ID, Permanent Resident Card, Certificate of Citizenship, Certificate of Naturalization, Employment Authorization Document, or foreign passport.
Documents by case (plus the signed application form): Algerian father, original nationality - applicant's, father's and grandfather's birth certificates. Father acquired nationality - applicant's birth certificate and copy of father's acquisition decree. Father's nationality proven by the judiciary - applicant's and father's birth certificates and executive copy of the final judicial decision. Algerian mother, original - applicant's birth certificate plus mother's nationality certificate, or mother's, her father's and her grandfather's birth certificates. Mother acquired - applicant's birth certificate and mother's acquisition decree. Mother proven by judiciary - applicant's and mother's birth certificates and the judicial decision. Unknown parents - full copy of Algerian birth certificate from the place of birth. Named mother only - same plus a certificate from the Directorate of Assisted Childhood. Judicial decision - applicant's birth certificate and executive copy of the decision.
All civil status documents must be in the national language and information must be consistent; the judicial authority may require corrections. Fee: free (per the official fee page).

title: Power of Attorney - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
Power of Attorney (Procuration) - Consulate General of Algeria in New York.
A legal document that appoints someone (procurator) to manage your personal or business affairs; you can define and limit their authority. Offered only to Algerian citizens, without prior appointment, for use in Algeria. Mail to 15 East 47th Street, New York, NY 10017.
Accepted identity documents: passport, national ID card, consular card, military card. Not accepted as proof of nationality: birth certificate, foreign ID documents, Algerian driver license.
In person: proxy form signed before a consular officer; original Algerian identity document; USPS money order of $6.25 ('Six Dollars and Twenty-Five Cents') per proxy.
By mail: proxy form signed and notarized before a notary public; notarized copy of the Algerian identity document; USPS money order of $6.25 per proxy; optional USPS Priority Mail return envelope.

title: Legalization of Documents - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
Legalization of Documents - Consulate General of Algeria in New York.
Commercial documents (for use in Algeria): original document signed by a company official and notarized by an official notary; authentication from the Department of State; translation into French or Arabic by an official translator; 'Seventy-Five Dollars USD ($75) USPS money order per each document'; the object of the contract or business transaction must be stated; certified return envelope if mailed.
Other documents: original and a copy of the document to be legalized; 'Two Dollars and Fifty Cents USD ($2.50) USPS money order'.
Hours: Tuesday to Saturday, 9 am to 3 pm; closed Sunday and Monday. No appointment needed.

title: National Service - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
National Service - Consulate General of Algeria in New York.
The census covers young Algerians born in the USA or elsewhere aged 17 or older registered with the consulate. 'Failure to enroll may result in the loss of the right of exemption, deferment, or deferral of incorporation.' File in person without appointment or by mail.
Census: enrollment form completed electronically and hand-signed by the legal guardian; one original Algerian birth certificate; self-addressed stamped envelope for the census certificate. Those who missed the census period are listed automatically according to the law.
Deferment (first-time or renewal): application form completed electronically; two 2x2 inch (51x51 mm) photos; copy of school transcript/enrollment or last diploma (school IDs not accepted); one original Algerian birth certificate ('12S is not acceptable'); prepaid USPS Priority return envelope.
Exemption: application form; two photos; one original Algerian birth certificate ('12S is not acceptable'); copy of last diploma or enrollment certificate; prepaid USPS Priority return envelope. Social reasons (e.g. soutien de famille): also original previous deferment document, letter to the Ministry of National Defense submitted under the authority of the Consulate, copy of parents' family record book, documents on brothers' national service position.
Lost exemption card replacement: application form; two photos; copy of the exemption if available; loss report form (notarized if mailed). Error correction: hand-signed letter; two photos; original Algerian birth certificate; original deferment or exemption card if available.
Request options: regularization, first-time deferment, deferment renewal, exemption for medical reasons, social reasons, presidential measures; age groups 17-18, 19-24, 25+. No fees stated.

title: Visa - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
Visas to Algeria - Consulate General of Algeria in New York.
Processes applications from residents of its 25-state jurisdiction. In person or by mail, no appointment; Tuesday through Friday 9:00 am to 3:00 pm (family visas also Saturday). Mail: 15 East 47th Street, New York, NY 10017. Form completed electronically, dated, hand-signed, one photo pasted. Every applicant including children and infants needs documents and fee. Applications with 'erasures, missing information or folded documents' are rejected. Under 18: birth certificate required. Generally issued within eight or ten days of receipt. Apply no more than sixty (60) days before travel. Submission does not guarantee a visa. Payment by Post Office (USPS) money order only. Include a Priority Mail Express return envelope.
Common documents: form; one recent standard photo; original passport and copy of photo page (valid at least 6 months, two blank pages); copy of proof of US legal residency; proof of address within the jurisdiction.
Type-specific: Tourist - hotel/travel agency booking or notarized invitation (host in Algeria via City Hall, or Algerian US resident host registered at CG New York), airline itinerary, proof of income - $160. Diplomatic/Official - diplomatic note, invitation if attending a meeting - $160. Press - employment letter, professional ID, equipment list, program (subject to MFA approval) - $160. Business - employer letter accepting financial responsibility, invitation from Algerian partner; holders may not work - $160. Student - acceptance letter, scholarship letter, proof of income - $160. Temporary Work (90 days or less) - employment contract, temporary work authorization from Algerian employment office, employer letter - $190. Cultural - invitation letter, proof of income (subject to MFA approval) - $190. Medical - medical certificate and letter from Algerian healthcare institution - $160. Work - work permit from Algerian employment office, employer letter - $190. Transit (max 7 days) - hotel reservation, itinerary, proof of income - $160. Family - copy of spouse's proof of Algerian nationality, marriage certificate - $160 (US passport). Fees above are for US passport holders. A family visa fee table without stated nationality also lists: multiple entries less than 90 days $33; multiple entries more than 90 days $66; other categories one entry (30 days) $110.

title: Consular Services Fees - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
Consular Services Fees - Consulate General of Algeria in New York.
Payment: USPS money orders only, exact amount, payable to 'Consulate-General of Algeria', with client's name and address; a separate money order per service with the service named in the memo. Not accepted: cash, personal or company checks, certified checks, bank or personal money orders, card payments.
Passport, students and children under 19: Standard (28 pages) $37.50; Large (48 pages) $56.25. Passport, employed or unemployed: Standard (28 pages) $75.00; Large (48 pages) $112.50. National identity card: old ID in possession - Free; old ID damaged or lost - $15.00. Visas to Algeria: varies by visa type and bilateral arrangements. Parental authorization for travel $2.50. Legalization of documents $2.50 per document. Certificate conform $2.50 per document. Certified copy $2.50 per document. Legalisation of commercial documents $75.00 per document. Certificate of origin for goods: increased by 400 DA per 10,000 DA of declared value (50% reduction for students and trainees only). Power of attorney $6.25 per proxy. Sworn statement $2.50 per document. Registration of vessels $312.50. Certificate of seaworthiness of vessels $375.00. Translation of a family record book $25.00. Duplicate of family book $25.00. Certificate of legal representative $6.25 (for each proxy). Translation $2.50. Declaration of loss $2.50. Certificate of life protection $2.50. Certificate of non-marriage, non-divorce and non-remarriage $2.50. Attestation of consular registration $2.50. Certificate of cancellation from the consular registers $2.50. Criminal record Free. Nationality Certificate Free. Consular card Free. 12-S Birth certificate Free.

title: Contact Us - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
Contact - Consulate General of Algeria in New York.
Address: 15 East 47th Street, New York, NY 10017. Phone: (212) 486-6930, (212) 486-6931, (212) 486-6932. Fax: (212) 486-6934. Hotline (green number): (917) 251-9795. Contact form on the site. 'All consular services are available without an appointment, EXCEPT FOR PASSPORTS.'

title: States of Jurisdiction - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
States of Jurisdiction - Consulate General of Algeria in New York (25 states): Alabama, Arkansas, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Vermont, Wisconsin.
Consulate General in San Francisco (19 states): California, Arizona, Nevada, Oregon, Washington, Utah, Colorado, Hawaii, Alaska, North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Oklahoma, Texas, Kansas, Wyoming, Montana, Idaho, New Mexico.
Embassy in Washington, D.C.: North Carolina, South Carolina, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia, West Virginia.

title: Opening Hours and Holidays - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text:
Opening hours - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. General consular services: Tuesday to Saturday, 9:00 am to 3:00 pm. Visa collection: Tuesday to Friday, 9:00 am to 3:00 pm. All consular services are available without an appointment, except passports.
Closed: Sunday and Monday (weekly); New Year's Day (January 1); Yennayer Day (January 12); Eid al-Fitr (three days); International Labor Day (May 1); Juneteenth Day (June 19); Eid al-Adha (three days); U.S. Independence Day (July 4); DZ Independence Day (July 5); Islamic New Year (one day); Mawlid al-Nabi Echarif (one day); Algeria Revolution Day (November 1); Veterans' Day (November 11); Thanksgiving Day (last Thursday in November); Christmas Day (December 25).

title: Appointments (RDV) - Consulate General of Algeria in New York
text: Appointments - Consulate General of Algeria in New York. 'All consular services are available without an appointment, EXCEPT FOR PASSPORTS.' The appointment page is an online booking form; if you do not receive the confirmation email within an hour, check your spam folder. Public hours: Tuesday to Saturday, 9 am to 3 pm; closed Sunday and Monday. Green number: (917) 251-9795.

title: File Transfer - Consulate General of Algeria in Brussels
text: FILE TRANSFER. Consulate General of Algeria in Brussels. "Consular file transfer is required in event of a change of a residency out of the consular jurisdiction." The request is made to the consulate covering the new area of residence. Algerian citizens who have newly settled in the consular jurisdiction of the Consulate General in Brussels are invited to submit their file transfer request to this office. Documents to submit: 1. Application form duly completed, dated and signed (downloadable from the page). 2. The consular card issued by the consulate holding the file, or a copy of the passport. 3. The residence permit, or the Belgian or Luxembourgish national identity card for dual citizens. 4. A recent proof of address. For any questions or special requests, contact immatriculation@consulatalgerie.be. Any changes in personal situation (profession, marriage, divorce, civil status) must also be notified to the Consulate. The page does not state fees, payment methods or processing times.

title: File Transfer - Consulate General of Algeria in Milan
text: FILE TRANSFER. Consulate General of Algeria in Milan. "Consular file transfer is required in event of a change of a residency out of the consular jurisdiction." The request is addressed to the consulate covering the new place of residence. Algerian citizens newly settled in the consular jurisdiction of Milan are invited to submit the following documents to the office: - "Application form duly completed, dated and signed to download"; - The consular card issued by the consulate holding the file, or a copy of the passport; - A residence permit, or a national identity card of the host country for dual citizens (the page text says French national identity card); - A recent proof of address. Notification of changes: "any changes in personal situation (profession, marriage, divorce, civil status) have to be notified to the Consulate." The page does not give fees, payment methods, step-by-step procedures or processing times; contact the consulate for these.

title: File Transfer - Consulate General of Algeria in London
text: FILE TRANSFER. Consulate General of Algeria in London. Algerian nationals already registered at an Algerian embassy or consulate abroad who now live permanently in the UK should "ask for the transfer of their Registration file." The Consulate handles the transfer, and the new registration at the London Consulate is granted once the file has arrived. "In some cases, the agreement of competent authorities in Algeria is needed." Required documents: 1. File transfer application form. 2. First registration application form. 3. (item missing in source numbering) 4. Original current consular registration card. 5. Original proof of legal, permanent residence in the UK. 6. Four recent passport-size photographs. 7. Any additional documents relating to your personal or professional background, if requested. The page does not state fees, payment, or processing times.

title: Consulate services - Consulate General of Algeria in London
text: Consulate services. Consulate General of Algeria in London. Main duties: the consulate is responsible to "identify, protect the interests, and provide assistance to all Algerian nationals" in its jurisdiction in the UK, in line with local law and policy, and acts as the link between them and Algeria. Services for the Algerian community: registers Algerians living in or visiting its jurisdiction; acts as civil registrar for births, marriages and deaths, and handles documents for the transfer of remains to Algeria; provides notarial services such as powers of attorney, kafala and successions; issues national identity cards, passports and emergency travel documents - only registered citizens qualify for all services except travel documents; handles military (national) service matters: registration (census), deferment and exemptions; provides consular protection in cases of arrest, imprisonment, serious accident or illness, and may assist with repatriation; informs on overseas voting rights, organizes elections and handles proxy voting; oversees economic, commercial, cultural and scientific relations with local authorities and institutions. Services for the foreign community: the consulate issues entry visas to Algeria for British citizens; other foreign nationals must provide proof of residence in the UK.

title: Is your passport ready? (online service) - Consulate General of Algeria in London
text: IS YOUR PASSPORT READY? Online service of the Consulate General of Algeria in London. Biometric passports are issued (handed over) Tuesday through Saturday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Applicants can check whether their biometric passport is ready by entering the application registration number shown on their deposit receipt (the page shows an image indicating where the number appears on the receipt). The online passport status check is available at services.mfa.gov.dz/fr/emblondon/passport. The page lists no fees or additional requirements.

title: Opening hours - Consulate General of Algeria in London
text: Opening hours. Consulate General of Algeria in London. The Consulate is "closed Sundays, Mondays and Algerian holidays." Passport service, civil status office (Etat civil) and other services: Tuesday to Saturday, 9:00 am to 3:00 pm. Visa section: Tuesday to Saturday; application lodging and collection from 9:30 am to 1:00 pm. Public holidays: New Year's Day (1 January); Amazigh New Year (12 January); Good Friday (date changes each year); Labour Day (1 May); Independence Day (5 July); Anniversary of the Revolution (1 November); Christmas Day (25 December); Boxing Day (26 December). Religious holidays: Eid al-Fitr (two days); Eid al-Adha (two days); Awal Muharram; Achoura; Mawlid al-Nabawi al-Sharif. Religious holiday dates follow the lunar calendar.

title: Contact - Consulate General of Algeria in London
text: Contact. Consulate General of Algeria in London (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and National Community Abroad). Phone: +44 (0)208 752 1177. Fax: +44 (0)208 752 8061. Toll-free (green number): 02087528066. Separate email addresses are listed for general information, visas, civil status, immigration, national service and consular matters. Opening hours: Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 15:00. Visa applications accepted Tuesday to Friday, 09:30 to 13:00. The contact page does not list the physical address or define the consular jurisdiction.

title: Emergency Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in London
text: Emergency Passport. Consulate General of Algeria in London. Legal basis: Executive Decree n° 16-58 of 3 February 2016 sets the conditions for issuing an Emergency Passport. The Emergency Passport is "exceptionally issued and delivered to the profit of Algerian citizens" whose immigration status regularization has been accepted by the receiving country and who need a valid passport. Application file: an Emergency Passport Application Form and a Description Form. "Note: The validity period of an Emergency Passport is one year running from its issuing date" and it cannot be extended or renewed. The page does not list fees, payment, steps or processing times.

title: Power of Attorney - Consulate General of Algeria in London
text: POWER OF ATTORNEY. Consulate General of Algeria in London. The power of attorney allows an Algerian citizen living in the UK to appoint someone to carry out an administrative or judicial procedure in Algeria on his/her behalf, for example buying or selling property or running a business. It cannot be used for marriage. The power of attorney is personal: the applicant must attend the Consulate in person. "Applications made by post are no longer accepted." Steps: 1. Complete the application form at the consulate. 2. Sign the form at the consulate in front of consular staff. Documents required - proof of identity, one of: consular registration card; passport; national identity card. "Other documents are not considered valid." Fee: £5. The applicant must be physically present for the Consulate to certify the document.

title: Transcription of Civil Records - Consulate General of Algeria in London
text: TRANSCRIPTION OF CIVIL RECORDS. Consulate General of Algeria in London. Scope: the London consulate registers births only for children born in the UK or Ireland; for births elsewhere, registration must be made at the Algerian embassy or consulate in the country of birth. Register an Algerian child's birth as soon as you receive the British or Irish birth certificate; do not delay. Application rules: incomplete applications are not accepted; incomplete postal applications may be ignored or returned. Postal applications must include a copy of your signed, valid consular registration card and a prepaid special or recorded delivery envelope for return of documents. Applicants in Ireland must include an £8 postal order for return postage, payable to the Algerian Consulate with your name written on the back; cheques are not accepted and cash must not be sent by post. Unregistered citizens must prove Algerian nationality and identity with an Algerian passport, a CNIA national identity card, or a military card with photo, and must complete the non-registered applicant form and provide two recent passport-size photos with their name on the back. In-person applications are accepted Tuesday to Saturday, mornings only, 9 am to 12 noon. Births registered in the same year as the child's birth get priority. Required documents (births in the UK or Ireland): 1. Application form completed in Arabic, dated and signed. 2. Original and copy of the full British or Irish birth certificate (short certificates are not accepted). 3. Family book (livret de famille), if you have one. 4. Copy of the applicant's consular registration card (registered citizens). 5. For unregistered citizens: proof of Algerian nationality and identity, the non-registered application form, and two passport-size photos. Processing time: depends on the number of applications and may take more than a month. Before applying for a child's passport, make sure the child is already registered; otherwise, provide the Algerian family book or the birth certificate issued by the Algerian embassy or consulate where the birth was registered.

title: Passport Renewal - Consulate General of Algeria in Milan
text: Passport Renewal. Consulate General of Algeria in Milan. Required documents (original and copy): - Valid consular registration card. - Passport application form, completed, dated and signed (available at the consulate or downloadable). - Photocopy of the first page of the expired passport. - Residence permit, or Italian identity card for dual nationals. - Proof of residence within the consular district. - Proof of activity. - Two identical identity photos. - Payment of the chancery fee. - Original 12S birth certificate plus a copy, for applicants renewing a passport issued by another consulate or in Algeria. Fees: adults €60; minor children, or students presenting a valid university education certificate, €30. When a passport can be renewed: "Less than six (06) months before expiration"; when the pages are nearly full of stamps (maximum of three pages left); in case of loss, theft or damage. The page does not state processing times or payment method.

title: Power of Attorney - Consulate General of Algeria in Milan
text: POWER OF ATTORNEY. Consulate General of Algeria in Milan. To have a power of attorney (procuration) issued, "the applicant must be present with a valid Algerian passport or identity card". Only a valid Algerian passport or national identity card is accepted as proof of identity. A downloadable application form is provided on the page. The page does not state fees, payment methods, steps or processing times; contact the consulate for these details.

title: Power of Attorney (Procuration) for the Algerian Citizen Only - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
text: Power of Attorney (Procuration) for Algerian Citizens Only. Embassy of Algeria in Washington, D.C. The Embassy issues this document so that Algerian citizens residing in its consular district can authorize a person living in Algeria to act and transact on their behalf. The applicant must "necessarily introduce his/her proxy in person". Walk-in requirements: - Completed application form, signed in front of a consular officer. - Original proof of identity: consular card, passport or national ID; no other documents are accepted. - USPS money order of $6.25 per proxy. Mail-in requirements: - Completed application form signed by the applicant and legalized by a public notary, with the notary's seal on the form. - Notarized copy of a valid Algerian ID (consular card, passport or national ID). - USPS money order of $6.25 per proxy. - Prepaid return envelope. Fee: $6.25 per proxy, payable by USPS money order only, made payable to the Embassy of Algeria. Processing time is not stated.

title: Consular pass declaration - Embassy of Algeria in Riyadh
text: Consular pass declaration (laissez-passer). Embassy of Algeria in Riyadh. The consular pass is issued to "non-resident Algerian citizens, who came on a visit visa" to Saudi Arabia and have lost their passport or whose passport has expired, allowing them to return to Algeria by the most direct route available. Required documents: - Proof of identity (passport or national identification card). - Copy of the entry visa to Saudi Arabia. - Passport loss certificate from the local authorities. - Three photos. - Confirmed travel ticket. The file is submitted to the consular office. Timing: submit the file "not less than a week and not more than 10 days" before departure. The transit document is issued only three days before departure. The page does not list fees or payment methods.

title: Consulate services - Consulate General of Algeria in Jeddah
text: Consulate services. Consulate General of Algeria in Jeddah. Passport, registration and change of residence: registers and re-registers nationals residing in the consular district and issues consular registration cards; accepts transfers of resident files from other consular posts; receives passport applications and renewals and performs biometric enrollment; delivers passports and national identity cards once produced in Algeria; issues change-of-residence certificates. Civil status: transcribes civil status documents; issues full copies for nationals born in the district; issues special 12S certificates for nationals transcribed in the Jeddah birth registers; issues certified extracts of civil status documents drawn up in Algeria or abroad upon presentation of the family record book. Legalization and certification: certifies powers of attorney and signatures of Algerian nationals; legalizes Algerian-issued deeds and documents and certifies copies; legalizes commercial documents; legalizes deeds issued by the host state and certifies copies. National service: receives national service files and delivers related documents. Social and legal: receives requests for criminal record extract no. 03 and issues it; receives driving licence capacity certificate applications, issued after preparation by the Algerian authority; handles the protection of Algerian nationals' interests under international conventions. Visa: processes visa applications. Hajj and Umrah: manages Hajj and Umrah files. Hours and contacts are not listed on this page.

title: Extracts of Civil Registration - Consulate General of Algeria in Istanbul
text: Extracts of Civil Registration. Consulate General of Algeria in Istanbul. The Consulate General notifies Algerian municipalities of civil status changes such as marriage and death. Changes made under judicial decisions of the host country are not recognized until the court of Sidi M'hamed (Algiers Judicial Council) issues an executive formula (exequatur) for them. Death certificate: the original authenticated death certificate; an identity document plus the deceased's birth certificate. Marriage certificate - to register (transcribe) a marriage contract with the Istanbul Consulate General, provide: the original marriage certificate; birth certificates of the husband and the wife; an Algerian nationality certificate for either spouse; a completed form; identity photos of both spouses. Birth certificate: the person concerned must hold Algerian nationality; the original certified birth certificate of the newborn; a clearly completed form; the family book (livret de famille) so the newborn can be added. The page does not specify fees, payment methods or processing times.

title: Emergency Passport - Consulate General of Algeria in Milan
text: Emergency Passport. Consulate General of Algeria in Milan. The emergency passport is a non-biometric, machine-readable travel document issued abroad by Algerian embassies and consulates, and in some cases by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Algiers. It is valid for 3 months to 1 year depending on the purpose, and cannot be extended. It is issued in emergencies and only exceptionally to: - Algerians living abroad, registered at a consular post, who have no passport and must travel urgently for family, professional, administrative or health reasons; - Algerians temporarily in a country other than their country of residence whose passport was lost, damaged, stolen or expired; - Algerians living abroad who are not registered at a consular post, whose residency file has been accepted by the host country, and who need a valid passport. Required documents: - A written request explaining the purpose of the application; - A document supporting the request; - The completed application form, signed by the applicant or, for minors, by the legal guardian; - Proof of Algerian nationality (e.g. passport copy, birth certificate, or form S12); - A copy of the consular registration card, for registered citizens; - Two recent, identical, unframed digital photos with a white background. Fees: 60 € stamp duty. If the passport was lost, stolen or destroyed: a police statement (declaration) from the local authorities and a 100 € loss fee. Steps: 1. Submit the application to the Consulate General at least one week in advance. 2. After review and acceptance, an appointment is scheduled. 3. At the appointment, bring the original documents that were sent by email. 4. The emergency passport must be returned when the biometric passport is issued and collected. Applications can be sent by email to biometrie@consulatgeneralalgeriemilan.it.

title: Opening hours - Consulate General of Algeria in Milan
text: Opening hours. Consulate General of Algeria in Milan. Consular services are available without an appointment. The office is open to the public Tuesday through Saturday, 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Visa services: application submission Tuesday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM; collection Tuesday to Friday, 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM. Applicants should check the section for their application type on the website to make sure their file is complete.

title: Opening hours - Consulate General of Algeria in Istanbul
text: Opening hours. Consulate General of Algeria in Istanbul. "Consular Services are delivered without appointments." Services run Monday to Friday, 9:00 am to 3:00 pm. Department phone numbers: Social Affairs and Document Authentication Department: +90 501 813 22 80. Civil Status Department: +90 501 813 22 78. Consular Registration and Biometric Documents Department: +90 501 813 22 79. Visa, Commercial, and Maritime Document Authentication Department: +90 501 086 11 80. On-Call and General Affairs Department: +90 501 813 22 77.

title: Transfer of remains of deceased citizens - Consulate General of Algeria in London
text: Transfer of remains of deceased citizens - Death & transfer of corpse. Consulate General of Algeria in London. The Consulate assists families of Algerian nationals who die abroad with preparing the remains and arranging their transfer to Algeria, in line with the family's wishes and local and Algerian regulations. "The Consulate does not pay the transfer of the remains." The Consulate should be contacted immediately after the death of an Algerian national so it can inform the family and give assistance and advice. A funeral service (undertaker) appointed by the family handles all administrative formalities; on request, the Consulate can recommend reliable undertakers. The Consulate informs the family and the relevant Algerian authorities of the death and the arrival date, and issues the death certificate and the "Authorisation de Transfert de corps". Documents required for the transfer authorisation: 1. Birth certificate (if the citizen is not registered at the Consulate). 2. Medical certificate "Free from infection" issued by the hospital or the doctor who certified the death. 3. Death certificate. 4. "Out of England" certificate issued by the Coroner. 5. Embalming certificate issued by the funeral services. 6. Undertaker's certificate confirming the coffin contains only the remains of the named deceased. 7. Certificate confirming the body was laid out according to Muslim rituals. 8. The deceased's identity documents, including the consular registration card. No fees or processing times are stated.

title: Consular Pass (Laissez-Passer) - Consulate General of Algeria in London
text: CONSULAR PASS - Travel document (Laissez-Passer). Consulate General of Algeria in London. "The Laissez-passer is a travel document issued in exceptional cases to enable the beneficiary to go back to Algeria." It cannot be used as an identity document, has very limited validity, and should only be used to enter Algeria on a direct flight. It is issued to Algerian citizens not registered at the Consulate who have reported their passport lost or stolen and wish to return to Algeria as soon as possible. Required documents: 1. Application form, completed and signed. 2. Declaration of passport loss. 3. Proof of Algerian nationality: original Algerian passport, national identity card, or military card with photograph (driving licences and birth certificates are not accepted). 4. Four recent photographs. 5. Travel ticket. Important notes: 1. If you cannot provide any of the documents above, you need a certified copy of one of them plus a declaration from two Algerian nationals registered at the Consulate confirming your nationality (downloadable form). 2. Applications for a voluntary return should be made "at least five (5) working days before the date of travel." Fees are not stated.

title: Exemption procedure (National Service) - Consulate General of Algeria in London
text: Exemption procedure - National Service. Consulate General of Algeria in London. Exemption from national service may be granted for the following reasons. 1. Ordinary application (applicants who have completed or abandoned their studies). Documents: completed, signed application form; original birth certificate, not an S12 extract (those born in the UK obtain it from the Consulate; those born in Algeria from the baladiya of birth); copy of the consular registration card; proof of UK residence (British passport, biometric residence permit, utility bill or bank statement); two passport-sized photographs; copy of an Algerian or British diploma, or, if studies were abandoned, the last school enrolment certificate; copy of a work contract or proof of paid work (e.g. payslips for the last three months). 2. Medical reasons: in addition to the above, evidence of the illness or physical or mental disability (medical certificates, X-rays if available, medical report). Documents in English must be translated into Arabic or French. 3. Social reasons (supporting the family, or other socially justified reason): in addition to the documents above, an application addressed to the Ministry of National Defence submitted through the Consulate; copy of the parents' family record book; father's death certificate, or parents' divorce certificate, or father's certificate of unemployment, retirement or disability, where applicable; copy of work contract or proof of paid work; documents showing the brothers' status regarding national service. 4. Algerian-French dual nationals: under the Algerian-French Agreement on National Service of 11 October 1983, exemption may be granted with the deferment or exemption documents above plus the "Déclaration d'Option" and "Certificat des Services" issued by the French military authorities. 5. Presidential measures: completed, signed application form; original birth certificate (not S12); current-year school enrolment certificate or work certificate; copy of consular registration card; four passport-sized photographs; proof of UK residence. Fees and processing times are not stated.

title: Census/Regularization (National Service) - Consulate General of Algeria in London
text: Census/Regularization - National Service. Consulate General of Algeria in London. Census: national service census is mandatory for Algerians who turn 17, live within the consulate's jurisdiction and are registered with it. "Failure to enrol shall involve the loss of the right of exemption, deferment, and deferral of incorporation." 1. Deferment (Sursis): open to citizens aged 19 or older; covers the full period of study and is renewed yearly until studies end or stop. First application: signed application form; original birth certificate, not an S12 extract (from the Consulate if born in the UK, from the Baladiya if born in Algeria); current-year school enrolment certificate; copy of consular registration card; four passport-sized photos; copy of proof of UK residence (residence card, British passport, biometric residence permit, utility bill or bank statement). Extension: signed application form; copy of consular registration card; original previous deferment certificate; current-year school enrolment certificate. Submit applications or extensions at the beginning of each academic year to avoid delays. 2. Deferral of incorporation (Report d'incorporation): granted if your brother is serving in or has been recalled to the army, or if you have a duly justified temporary impediment; provide the same documents as for deferment plus evidence supporting the reason. Bring photocopies of the required documents to speed up processing.

title: Criminal Record - Consulate General of Algeria in Istanbul
text: CRIMINAL RECORD. Consulate General of Algeria in Istanbul. "Algerian citizens registered with the services of the Algerian Consulate in Istanbul and born in Algeria" can obtain criminal record certificate (casier judiciaire) No. 03 directly from the Consulate General. Foreign nationals who have lived in Algeria are also eligible. Applications are submitted in person. Required: 1. Completed criminal record certificate request form. 2. Birth certificate, if born in Algeria. 3. Algerian citizens: Algerian identity card. 4. Foreign nationals: identity card and any document proving former residence in Algeria. Fees and processing times are not stated.

title: Travel Document (Laissez Passer) - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
text: Travel Document (Laissez Passer). Embassy of Algeria in Washington, D.C. The laissez-passer is a "temporary travel document issued to Algerian nationals who are not registered at the Algerian Embassy" to allow them to return to Algeria after their passport was lost, stolen or expired. It is also issued to newborns in the U.S. whose Algerian parents are visiting on a tourist visa or lack legal immigration status. It is valid for 30 days and only for a one-way trip to Algeria by the shortest route. Required documents: completed, signed laissez-passer application form; two recent passport-size photographs; confirmed flight ticket; self-addressed return envelope (only if the document will be mailed). Adults: proof of Algerian nationality - Algerian passport (if available), or Algerian National ID or Military ID card with photo; if the passport is damaged, submit the damaged passport; if lost or stolen, submit a Lost or Stolen Passport Form. Newborns and minors: proof of Algerian nationality of at least one parent (e.g. passport); original full-version birth certificate of the child; if the father is not present at the Embassy, an authorization letter from him - notarized if applying by mail, or legalized by a Commune administrative officer if he is in Algeria. Civil status documents and foreign documents are not accepted as proof of nationality. "The laissez-passer request must be submitted at least 72 hours before departure."

title: Other Services (legalization, parental authorization, kafala, casier judiciaire, J-1 waiver) - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
text: Other services. Embassy of Algeria in Washington, D.C. 1. US-issued documents (legalization): the original document must be notarized, carry the apostille of the issuing state, and be certified by the U.S. Department of State; include a photocopy; fee $75 (non-refundable) USPS money order per document; include a prepaid return envelope. 2. Travel document (laissez-passer): issued in exceptional cases to return to Algeria; not an identity document; valid 30 days only; requirements: application form, declaration of passport loss, proof of Algerian nationality (national ID card or military card with photo; driving licences and birth certificates not accepted), four recent photographs, travel ticket. 3. Minor child travel (parental authorization): an Algerian minor aged 19 or younger travelling without his parents needs a notarized travel authorization signed by the father, which border authorities may require. Not required if the parents are divorced or separated, the minor lives abroad with the mother, and the mother holds a court order granting full custody (to be shown when leaving Algeria). Requirements: application form; original and copy of the minor's full birth certificate or family book; father's consular card, national ID or passport; money order (fee listed as $2.50). Valid three months. The father or guardian must be present; if the father or both parents are deceased, a parent or guardian must be present. A mother travelling with the child must provide her residence card, a copy of the custody document, proof of the child's legal presence abroad and the family booklet. 4. Power of attorney (procuration), Algerian citizens only: in person - form signed before a consular officer, original consular card/passport/national ID, $6.25 USPS money order per proxy; by mail - notarized form with notary seal, notarized copy of valid Algerian ID, $6.25 USPS money order per proxy, prepaid return envelope. 5. Transfer of property in an estate: property (including vehicles) must have been fully owned by the deceased; assets must be repatriated within one year of the date the "Fredha" was established; applicant must be authorized by the heirs and hold a notarized special power of attorney; documents: dated and signed inventory of the estate legalized by consular services ($7.50 stamp duty), notarized copy of the Fredha deed, death certificate, special power of attorney, customs declaration for release for consumption. 6. Legal adoption (Kafala): age limits 60 for men and 55 for women; single, widowed and divorced women may apply under similar conditions; the Kafil must be in good health, Muslim, of Algerian nationality, with suitable accommodation; documents: written request with reasons, both spouses' birth certificates, family form, medical certificates, criminal records from the country of residence, work certificate, three months of pay stubs, copy of consular card, property title or lease; all documents translated into Arabic or French. 7. Judicial records (Casier Judiciaire No. 3): for Algerians abroad and foreign nationals who lived in Algeria; requirements: original full birth certificate, valid ID, proof of residence in Algeria (foreign nationals only), self-addressed prepaid envelope, signed application form. 8. Waiver (Attestation de Non-Objection) for J-1 visa holders subject to the two-year home-residence requirement (INA 212(e)): copy of consular registration card; copy of the J-1 waiver recommendation application (all pages); notarized affidavit confirming no obligations to any Algerian public or private entity; job offer on the institution's letterhead. 9. Elections: to be on the electoral roll a citizen must be registered at the embassy, be 18 on Election Day and enjoy civil and political rights; ordinary reviews at the end of each year, exceptional reviews when an election is announced. Contact: (202) 265-2800 or consular-section@algerianembassy.org.

title: Biometric Passport - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
text: Biometric Passport. Embassy of Algeria in Washington, D.C. Biometric passports are issued only after consular registration is completed. Children under 12 do not need to be fingerprinted in person or collect the passport at the consulate; all documents are sent by mail. Applicants 12 and older must visit for fingerprinting (no appointment needed); mailing the application first can speed up the process. Renewals should be submitted at least six months before the current passport expires. Passports are produced in Algeria and take several weeks; you can track your application one week after fingerprinting with your receipt number. Required documents: completed application form (signed by the legal guardian if applicable); one passport photo meeting size, background and pose requirements; S12 birth certificate, only if your previous biometric passport was not issued by the Embassy in Washington; copy of a valid consular registration card; current or expired passport - if lost or damaged, a Passport Lost or Stolen Form and a penalty fee (lower for students and minors); proof of legal U.S. residency (U.S. passport, Green Card or appropriate visa); proof of employment or school enrollment; proof of U.S. address (utility bill or lease); prepaid USPS Priority Mail return envelope with tracking number. Fees: 28-page passport - adults (19+) $75.00, minors and students $37.50; 48-page passport - adults $112.50, minors and students $56.25. Payment: only U.S. Postal Service money orders, payable to "Embassy of Algeria"; no other payment methods accepted.

title: Consular Registration (consular card) - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
text: Consular Registration. Embassy of Algeria in Washington, D.C. "The Embassy of Algeria urges Algerian citizens residing permanently abroad to complete their consular registration." Registration is required for passport issuance and voter registration. Algerian citizens aged 19 and over can apply and receive a consular card valid for five years. Married Algerian women may, where applicable, be registered under their husband's file. Children under 19 are generally registered under a parent's file. The consular card is free of charge. Applications can be made in person without an appointment, or by mail to the Embassy in Washington, D.C. (The page refers to a personalised checklist of documents.)

title: Consular registration and other services - Embassy of Algeria in Abu Dhabi
text: Consular registration. Embassy of Algeria in Abu Dhabi. Registration is for citizens who are regular residents; it allows the embassy to locate citizens and provides consular protection, easier access to administrative documents, and a one-time certificate of change of residence for moving belongings and a tourist car upon final return. Documents: original birth certificate; original father's birth certificate; nationality certificate (or the father's and grandfather's birth certificates for those born in Algeria); passport copy; copy of valid UAE (Abu Dhabi) residence permit; five identical recent photos; work certificate, or university certificate for students; family situation: marriage contract (married), copy of divorce judgment (divorced), or husband's death certificate (widowed). The applicant must appear in person. The registration card is free and valid five years. Renewal of the card is required after a change in civil status, profession or residence: expired card, document reflecting the change, two recent photos; attendance required. Re-registration: citizens who obtained a certificate of change of residence or requested a deletion certificate must register again under the same conditions as a first registration. Elections: voter cards are issued to citizens on the electoral roll (registered at the embassy, 18 on Election Day, enjoying civil and political rights); ordinary review yearly from 1 to 31 October; exceptional review when an election is announced. Power of attorney (procuration), Algerian citizens only, in person: completed form signed before a consular officer; original consular card, passport or national ID; postal money order payable to the Embassy for each proxy. Judicial records (Casier Judiciaire No. 3): original full birth certificate, valid ID, proof of residence in Algeria (foreign nationals), self-addressed prepaid envelope, signed application form. Laissez-passer: exceptional, not an identity document, valid 30 days; application form, declaration of passport loss, proof of nationality (national ID or military card with photo; driving licence and birth certificate not accepted), four recent photos, travel ticket. Minor child travel: a minor aged 19 or younger travelling without a parent needs a notarized parental travel authorization signed by the father (not required where the mother holds a court order granting full custody and the child lives abroad with her); documents: form, child's full birth certificate or family book, father's consular card/ID/passport, money order; valid three months; father or guardian must attend. National military service: registration required at age 18; citizens who applied for deferment or exemption cards should contact the Office of Consular Affairs. (Note: some text on this page appears copied from the Washington embassy template.)

title: Contact - Embassy of Algeria in Abu Dhabi
text: Contact. Embassy of Algeria in Abu Dhabi. Phone: 0097124448949. Fax: 0097124447068. Email: ambalg@embassy-algeria-uae.com (general); cultural@embassy-algeria-uae.com; economic@embassy-algeria-uae.com. Working hours - Consular Department: Sunday to Wednesday, 9:00 a.m. to 2:30 p.m.; Thursday, 9:00 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. Other embassy services: Sunday, 11:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; Monday to Thursday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Address: Zayed the First Street, Electra, behind the Holiday Inn Hotel, Building 05, Abu Dhabi. For emergencies, a toll-free number is indicated.

title: Transferring the body of a deceased Algerian citizen abroad - Embassy of Algeria in Riyadh
text: Transferring the body of a deceased Algerian citizen abroad. Embassy of Algeria in Riyadh. If an Algerian citizen dies abroad, relatives must submit a file to the consular services to obtain a permit to transport the body. The file must include: a death certificate from the Civil Status Department; a burial permit; an embalming certificate; a transfer authorization; and a certificate of absence of contagious disease. Fees and processing times are not stated.

title: Consular registration - Embassy of Algeria in Berlin
text: Consular registration. Embassy of Algeria in Berlin. "Consular registration is an administrative procedure concerning Algerian nationals" legally residing abroad; it is required to receive consular protection and services. First registration: appear in person at the consulate covering your place of residence. Minors under 19 are registered at the request of the person holding parental authority; for divorced parents, the divorce judgment must be presented. Documents for first registration: completed, dated and signed application form (Forms section); Algerian passport or national identity card, with photocopy of the first three passport pages and the pages showing German entry visas; Algerian nationality certificate, or alternative birth certificates if unavailable; naturalization decree if Algerian nationality was acquired; residence permit (or renewal receipt) or valid national identity card of the host country, with photocopy; proof of address dated within the last three months, with photocopy; for people staying with a host, a sworn statement from the host legalized by the local town hall plus the host's proof of address; proof of employment with photocopy; four recent passport photos (3.5 x 4.5 cm); marriage certificate or family booklet if married; divorce judgment (original and copy) for divorced women. Spouses and minor children are registered as dependents; a spouse provides the same documents plus a marriage certificate. Minors: birth certificate (full copy if born in Algeria, transcribed extract if born abroad); residence permit or national ID with photocopy; two recent identical photos; the father or legal guardian must be present. Card renewal: the consular card is valid five years; submit the expired card, two recent colour photos from the same series, residence permit and photocopy, and a new registration certificate if the address changed. Moving to another consular district: present your consular card, registration certificate and valid residence permit at the new consulate. Report any change of civil status, address or occupation with supporting documents. Removal from the register: upon death, permanent return to Algeria, change of consular district, handwritten request, or absence exceeding 10 years; removal also removes you from the electoral roll. Fees: consular registration card free of charge; removal certificate subject to a stamp fee.

title: Other services (laissez-passer, parental authorization, casier judiciaire, procuration, national service) - Embassy of Algeria in Berlin
text: Other services. Embassy of Algeria in Berlin. Travel document (laissez-passer): issued in exceptional cases to return to Algeria; "It cannot be used as an identity document"; valid 30 days only. Required: application form; declaration of passport loss; proof of Algerian nationality (national ID or military card with photo; driving licence and birth certificate not accepted); four recent photographs; travel ticket. Minor child travel (parental authorization): Algerian minors aged 19 or younger travelling without their parents need a notarized travel authorization signed by the father; not required if the parents are divorced or separated, the minor lives abroad with the mother and she holds a court order granting full custody. Required: application form; original and copy of the full birth certificate or family book; father's consular card, national ID or passport; money order. Valid three months; the father or guardian must be present. For the custody exemption, the mother provides her residence card, copy of the custody document, proof of the child's legal residence or schooling abroad, and the family booklet or other proof of family ties. Judicial records (Casier Judiciaire No 3): for Algerians abroad and foreign nationals who lived in Algeria; original full birth certificate, valid ID, proof of residence in Algeria (foreign nationals), self-addressed prepaid envelope, signed application form. Power of attorney (procuration), Algerian citizens only: applicant appears in person; form signed before the consular officer; original consular card, passport or national ID; postal money order payable to the Embassy for each proxy. Elections: registered citizens receive a voting card (must be registered at the Embassy, 18 on Election Day, with civil and political rights); ordinary review every year from 1 to 31 October; exceptional review when an election is announced. National military service: citizens who applied for deferment or exemption cards should contact Consular Affairs; registration is required at age 18. (Note: parts of this page reproduce the Washington embassy template text.)

title: Consular Registration - Consulate General of Algeria in Geneva
text: CONSULAR REGISTRATION. Consulate General of Algeria in Geneva (page as published; its jurisdiction line names Bas-Rhin (67), Haut-Rhin (68) and Vosges (88), apparently copied from the Strasbourg consulate template). Consular registration is an administrative procedure for Algerian citizens regularly residing abroad. "The consular registration card is issued free of charge." It is valid five years and renewal must be requested. Changes in civil status, address or profession must be reported with supporting documents. Registered persons who definitively return to Algeria must request removal from the consular registers. First registration (originals plus A4 photocopies): completed, dated and signed application form; Algerian passport with copies of the first three pages, visa page and Schengen entry page; birth certificate (12 S) with copy; father's full birth certificate (if born in Algeria), or father's and grandfather's full birth certificates (if born abroad); naturalization decree if applicable; proof of family status (family record book, marriage certificate or divorce judgment); residence permit with an address in the jurisdiction, renewal receipt, or valid national ID card; recent proof of residence (under three months) or accommodation certificate legalized by the city hall; proof of activity (work certificate, payslip, scholarship certificate, unemployment notice, disability or retirement notice); five recent passport photos 3.5 x 4.5 cm. Spouses and minor children are registered as dependents; the spouse submits the same documents. Minors: legal guardian's registration card; child's 12 S birth certificate with copy; DCEM or national ID card for dual citizens; two recent photos; "The presence of the legal guardian is mandatory." Renewal: expired card; completed form; proof of regular stay with copy; proof of residence with copy if the address changed; two recent photos; work certificate, payslips or attendance certificate for students and trainees. Re-registration (after a certificate of change of residence, personal request, or absence of more than 10 years): same documents as the initial registration.

title: National Military Service - Embassy of Algeria in Riyadh
text: National Military Service. Embassy of Algeria in Riyadh. Requests for registration (census), postponement (deferment) or exemption are submitted to the consular authority, which forwards them to the competent authorities in Algeria; applicants are notified when responses arrive. Registration: "Those concerned should approach the consular authority before December 01, 2027" - this concerns the class of 2027, i.e. Algerian citizens residing abroad born in 2007. Documents: completed registration form; birth certificate; two photos; copy of the legal guardian's consular registration card. Postponement: written request; copy of passport; copy of residence document; copy of consular card; justification (usually a university certificate); copies of previous postponement certificates, if any. Exemption: written request; copy of passport; copy of residence card; copy of consular card; justification depending on the reason (work certificate, medical report, or file of an only son supporting the family); copies of previous postponement certificates, if any; four photos. No fees are listed.

title: Consular registration (first registration, renewal, transfer, deletion) - Embassy of Algeria in Washington
text: Consular registration. Embassy of Algeria in Washington, D.C. First registration - documents: signed application form; original full birth certificate; original birth or death certificate of the applicant's father; if born abroad, birth certificates of two paternal ancestors born in Algeria, or a certificate of Algerian nationality; marriage certificate if married; record of divorce judgment if divorced; copy of proof of legal presence in the US (long-stay visa, green card or US passport - photocopy of the passport's first page and US visa page); proof of address within the Embassy's consular district; statement of employment or university registration; three recent passport-size photos (frontal, same batch, unedited, white background, no glasses except prescription), with first and last names written in pencil on the back. Notice: the applicant must appear in person with the original proof of legal presence in the US. The registration card is valid five years and must then be renewed (Art. 19, Presidential Decree 02-405 of 2002); failure to renew within ten years results in removal from the register (Art. 20). Renewal - documents: signed application form; expired registration card (if lost, stolen or damaged, a signed declaration of loss notarized with the notary's seal and a $2.50 penalty paid by US Postal Service money order only, payable to the Embassy of Algeria); two passport-size photos; copy of proof of legal presence in the US; proof of address within the consular district; statement of employment or university registration; self-addressed prepaid envelope. The applicant must sign the registration card when it arrives by mail. Transfer of consular registration - documents: signed application form; original consular registration card; two passport-size photos; copy of proof of legal presence (visa, green card or US passport); proof of address within the consular district; statement of employment or school registration; the applicant must appear in person with the original proof of legal presence. Deletion from the consular register (Art. 36, Presidential Decree 02-405, with Arts. 26-27): death; final return to Algeria; change of consular district; handwritten request for cancellation; absence of more than 10 years. Deletion also removes the person from the electoral roll. A fee is charged for a certificate of deletion (amount not stated).

title: Loi n° 02-01 du 5 février 2002 relative à l'électricité et à la distribution du gaz par canalisations
text:
Loi n° 02-01 du 22 Dhou El Kaada 1422 correspondant au 5 février 2002 relative à l'électricité et à la distribution du gaz par canalisations. Consumer-relevant provisions by article.

1. Access to electricity and gas.
