title: SNTF – Avantages tarifaires
text:
SNTF (Société Nationale des Transports Ferroviaires) – Fare reductions and travel cards.

Children: under 4, free if carried on an accompanying adult's knees. Ages 4 to 12: half fare (50% off) with a separate seat.

Carte Jeune (youth card): 20% off ticket purchases. Valid 1 year from issue. Named card for ages 15 to 28. Routes over 100 km: Algiers suburban, regional and long-distance (grandes lignes) services. Application: submit to the station master (chef de gare) a handwritten request, a civil status document (extrait d'acte de naissance) and two ID photos (one for the card, one for the file). Issued within one day. Fee: 60 DA.

Carte Famille Nombreuse (large family card): 30% off, second class only. Valid 3 years. For families with at least 3 unmarried children under 18; requested by the head of family. Routes: regional and long-distance services. Application: a special form available at the station, signed by the head of family, plus photos, family record book (livret de famille), birth certificates, and an official document proving the nationality of the head of family and spouse. Issued within 10 days. Fee: 100 DA regardless of how many cards are issued; duplicates charged per card.

Carte 3ème Âge (senior card): 20% off each ticket. Valid for life. Eligibility: women 55 and older, men 60 and older. Routes over 100 km: Algiers suburban, regional and long-distance. Application at ticket counters with an ID document and one photo. Issued within one day. Fee: 60 DA.

Persons with reduced mobility: free or reduced tickets depending on disability rate, on presentation of the card issued by the wilaya Social Action services (DAS).

Ordinary tickets: one-way full fare; for trips of at least 200 km interrupted en route, the ticket is valid 5 days (Fridays and holidays included) if endorsed at the station where the journey was interrupted. Round trip: 20% off for trips over 400 km (aller-retour), valid 2 months.

Subscriptions (abonnements):
- Ordinary (named, 35% off, second class, routes up to 200 km): 1 month, 3 months or 1 year. Monthly includes 15 free days of travel; annual includes 5 free months. Apply on the rail form at least 8 days ahead at any station, with ID, a photocopy of ID, and payment. Consignment fee: 50 DA. Duplicates charged per card.
- Weekly suburban (Annaba, Constantine, Oran only): 30% off, 1 week.
- Monthly suburban (Annaba, Constantine, Oran only): 40% off, 1 month.
- Carte Verte (Algiers suburban railcars): 30% off weekly; 40% off monthly, quarterly, semi-annual and annual. Annual cards can be paid in 3 instalments.
- Half-fare cards (cartes demi-tarif): issued on request at the Regional Rail Directorate headquarters, for 3, 6 or 12 months; annual cards payable in 3 instalments. Card A: half-fare tickets in first or second class at the traveller's choice. Card B: half-fare tickets in second class only.

Group travel:
- Ordinary groups of 10 or more on a round trip: 30% off, for trips up to 300 km round trip. Children 4 to 12 pay half the adult price.
- Sports groups (affiliated with national or foreign federations): 30% off for 10+, 40% off for 31+, 50% off for 61+.
- Summer camps (colonies de vacances): groups of 10+ under age 21 get 50% off full single fares; 75% when organised at the exclusive cost of communes or charitable organisations.

Upgrades: to move to a higher class, declare it to the train chief or inspector first and pay the difference between two single fares; otherwise the traveller is irregular.

Ticket checks and irregular travel: tickets must be shown on request and returned at the end of the trip (or exchanged for a service note). A traveller is irregular if they have no ticket, an expired or altered ticket, no return coupon, travel beyond the ticket's distance/route without notice, or travel in a higher class without notice. Without fraud, the traveller can avoid prosecution by paying a flat indemnity plus the fare difference on the spot. If not paid on the train, they are removed at the first major stop and handed to the station chief, and owe the fare plus double the flat indemnity.

title: CREG – التسعيرة (Tarifs de l'électricité et du gaz)
text:
لجنة ضبط الكهرباء والغاز (CREG) – التسعيرة. Electricity and gas tariffs page.

Legal basis: tariffs are governed by Law No. 02-01 of 5 February 2002 on electricity and gas distribution through pipelines (القانون رقم 02-01 المؤرخ في 5 فبراير 2002).

Setting authority: CREG set electricity and gas tariffs under decision No. D/22-15/CD of 29 December 2015. The tariffs took effect on 1 January 2016 and are expressed excluding taxes (hors taxes).

Uniformity: the tariffs are "موحدة في جميع انحاء التراب الوطني" (uniform throughout the national territory).

Cost components: for electricity, the tariff covers production, transport, distribution and marketing; for natural gas, transport, distribution and marketing.

The detailed tariff tables (tiers and prices per kWh / thermie) are published on the page as images: electricity table https://creg.gov.dz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Capture-5.png and gas table https://creg.gov.dz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Capture-2.png (not transcribed here). CREG also offers an online bill estimator (تقدير فاتورتك) at https://mouhakat.creg.dz/.

Contact: CREG, Section 04, Groupe de propriété 788, Zone d'activité, Immeuble Chéraga, Alger. Tel +213 28 91 03 01 / +213 28 91 03 02. Email contact@creg.gov.dz.

title: CREG – تقديم طعن (Recours des consommateurs)
text:
تقديم طعن لدى لجنة ضبط الكهرباء والغاز (CREG)

المرجع القانوني: تنص المادة 115 من القانون رقم 02-01 المؤرخ في 5 فبراير 2002 على أن اللجنة تسهر على حماية مصالح المستهلكين وصون حقوقهم في التزويد وجودة الخدمة واستمراريتها، وتستقبل شكاواهم وطلبات الطعن وتدرسها وفق الإجراءات المعمول بها.

1. الحالات التي يمكن فيها التوجه إلى اللجنة (عند وجود نزاع مع الموزِّع):
- عدم معالجة طلب ربط أو تعديله، أو التأخر في إنجازه.
- عدم معالجة طلب تحويل منشأة، أو التأخر في إنجازه.
- عدم معالجة مشكلة تتعلق بالانقطاع أو الإصلاح أو السلامة.
- الاعتراض على فاتورة الطاقة (مبلغ مفرط، مؤشر خاطئ، استهلاك غير صحيح، إلخ).
- طلب تعديل عقد التزويد (التعريفة، القدرة، التدفق، إلخ).
- طلب إعادة التزويد بعد قطعه بسبب عدم التسديد.
- انخفاض التوتر أو الضغط.
- المشاكل المرتبطة بالعداد.
- حقوق المتابعة (الحصة الجزئية).
- التعويض عن الحوادث.

2. الإجراءات المسبقة لدى الموزِّع: يجب تقديم كل شكوى تقنية أو تجارية أو إدارية أولاً إلى موزِّع الكهرباء والغاز وفق إجراءاته الداخلية لمعالجة الشكاوى المعتمدة من اللجنة. الموزِّع: الشركة الجزائرية لتوزيع الكهرباء والغاز (SADEG)، مبنى 500 مكتب، الطريق رقم 38، وادي قسنطينة، الجزائر؛ الهاتف 021.83.55.00؛ الموقع www.sonelgaz-distribution.dz. يمكن الاستعانة بإحدى جمعيات حماية المستهلك (القائمة على موقع وزارة التجارة).

3. متى يمكن تقديم الطعن؟ إذا لم تتلقَّ ردّاً من الموزِّع في أجل أقصاه ثلاثة (03) أشهر، أو إذا كان الرد غير مرضٍ. يجب إرفاق الطعن بالوثائق الثبوتية، مثل نسخ جميع المراسلات الموجهة إلى الموزِّع وردوده إن وُجدت.

4. كيفية تقديم الطعن: عبر الإنترنت بملء الاستمارة الإلكترونية أو عبر منصة "إلتماس" (iltimess.creg.dz)؛ أو بتحميل الاستمارة الورقية وإيداعها بمقر اللجنة (من الأحد إلى الخميس، 09:00–16:00)، أو إرسالها بالبريد إلى: لجنة ضبط الكهرباء والغاز، القسم 04، المجموعة الملكية 788، منطقة النشاط، عمارة الشراقة، الجزائر؛ أو بالفاكس 028 91 03 02؛ أو بالبريد الإلكتروني recours@creg.gov.dz.

5. مسار المعالجة: تدرس اللجنة القبول والاختصاص في أجل أقصاه ثلاثة (03) أيام عمل، ثم تُعلمكم إن كان الطعن خارج الاختصاص أو غير مقبول (عدم استنفاد الإجراءات المسبقة، ملف ناقص، نزاع أمام القضاء). في حال القبول تطلب اللجنة من الموزِّع التوضيحات وتدعوه إلى الرد خلال خمسة عشر (15) يوماً. إذا كانت حجج الموزِّع مبررة تُرسل اللجنة رسالة توضيحية وتغلق الملف؛ وإذا كانت غير مبررة تطالبه بالامتثال، فإن رفض تتخذ اللجنة قراراً لصالحكم يُبلَّغ للطرفين. يمكن للجنة جمع الأطراف لتسوية ودية. يبقى لكل طرف حق اللجوء إلى الجهات القضائية المختصة.

6. الاتصال: الهاتف +213 28 91 03 01 / +213 28 91 03 02؛ contact@creg.gov.dz؛ الطعون recours@creg.gov.dz.

title: CCP / e-CCP - Algérie Poste
text:
Algérie Poste – CCP (compte courant postal) and e-CCP services for individuals.

1. CCP account

Opening an account (individuals): provide a copy of a valid ID document and either a residence certificate (certificat de résidence) or a certificate of presence in the military or paramilitary corps (attestation de présence). Submit the account application form "CH1" and sign the two signature specimens on form "CH 25", available at the post office. Legal entities must go to the main receipt office (recette principale) of the chef-lieu de wilaya or the company service.

Changing address: submit a request on plain paper or form "CH18", with a copy of valid ID and a residence certificate for the new address (or a certificate of presence for military and paramilitary personnel).

Changing the account name: use form "CH4" with supporting documents: name change – copy of the court judgment; spelling correction of a name or first name – copy of the court judgment; marriage of a woman – copy of the marriage certificate; divorce – copy of the court judgment.

Changing signature: sign the two "CH 25" specimens with the new signature.

Cash withdrawals (paiements à vue): withdrawals can be made at any post office using a CCP cheque or form "SFP1", together with the CCP withdrawal card. Withdrawals are capped at 200,000 DA per day. Above 200,000 DA, the client must place a fund reservation, which is fulfilled within 48 hours at most.

Withdrawals on sight without balance check: up to 30,000 DA can be withdrawn at the office holding the signature specimen ("CH 25 bis"), in exchange for a cheque payable to the office head, by the account holder or their authorised representative (mandataire).

Deposits (versements): made at any post office with valid ID, using CCP mandats "1418" or accelerated deposit ("VAC").

Balance inquiry: at any post office by submitting form "SFP1" with ID, or by presenting a cheque and the account holder's ID. Balance can also be checked by phone (dial "15-30"), by SMS to "603", or online via the e-CCP service.

Account statement (relevé): requested at any post office or online via the e-CCP site. The period cannot exceed 24 months.

Closing an account: the account holder submits a handwritten request at a post office, the CNCP (Centre National des Chèques Postaux) or a CFR (Centre Financier Régional). Heirs submit a handwritten request with a copy of the death certificate at a post office, the CNCP or a CFR.

Ordering a cheque book: at a post office, submit the completed insert found in the middle of the cheque book, or order "code 3" to receive it at the office of your choice; online via e-ccp.poste.dz for holders of a confidential access code; or by phone by dialling "15-30" and following the prompts.

Receiving a cheque book: the client is notified by an arrival notice sent to their home address, or by SMS if subscribed to SMS notifications.

2. e-CCP account

The web service lets users check their CCP balance, view and download their account statement, change their confidential code, and order a cheque book. To use it, obtain a confidential code at any post office by presenting a copy of valid ID. The service is at https://eccp.poste.dz/.

title: CREG – Droits et Obligations des consommateurs
text:
CREG (Commission de Régulation de l'Électricité et du Gaz) – Rights and obligations of electricity and gas consumers (owners or tenants of a dwelling) towards the distributor.

Your rights as an owner or tenant:
- Obtain an electricity or gas connection where a network exists.
- Be welcomed, advised and assisted by the distributor.
- Receive four invoices per year.
- Be informed of connection conditions and timelines, tariffs and payment methods.
- Be informed of internal and external appeal (recours) options.
- Receive advance notice of scheduled outages, including dates and times.
- Receive answers to all your complaints.
- Be compensated if your equipment is damaged by outages or voltage drops.
- Be compensated when the distributor's structures or lines cross your property.

Your obligations toward the distributor:
- Pay your energy bill by the due date printed on it.
- Keep your indoor installations compliant with safety standards and good practice.
- Give the distributor easy, permanent access to your meter and installations.
- Refuse any fraudulent connections made from your installations.
- Contact the distributor before starting work near its facilities.
- Do not tamper with your meters.

Contact CREG: +213 28 91 03 01 / 02, contact@creg.gov.dz. Complaints (recours): recours@creg.gov.dz.

title: CREG – Comment lire votre facture
text:
CREG – How to read your electricity and gas bill (Sonelgaz / SADEG).

Invoice header: invoice number and issue date; consumption-place reference (a unique number assigned by the distributor) and consumption address; expected date of the next meter reading.

Distributor (SADEG – Société Algérienne de Distribution de l'Électricité et du Gaz): logo and share capital, responsible distribution directorate and local commercial agency; identifiers RC, NIS, NIF, RIB and RIP.

Customer: customer number and name of the consumption-place owner; RC and NIF for non-household customers.

Call centre: 33 03, for assistance, breakdowns, complaints and information requests.

Billing period: one quarter, covering three months of consumption.

Meter and tariff codes: the meter number is the last four digits shown at the bottom of the meter. Electricity: 54M (household, four tiers) and 54NM (non-household, three tiers). Gas: 23M (household, four tiers) and 23NM (non-household, three tiers).

Subscribed power (PMD) and flow (DMD): PMD is chosen from standard values – single-phase 220 V at 4, 6 or 12 kW; three-phase 380 V at 20, 40, 60 or 80 kW. DMD is the hourly gas flow: 16 Nm³/h on a low-pressure network, or 25 Nm³/h on a medium-pressure network.

Coefficient: electricity 1; gas: the calorific value (PCS), which converts cubic metres to thermies (Th).

Meter readings: old and new indexes, ignoring decimals. Letter beside them: R – actual reading by the distributor's agent; E – estimate based on consumption history (meter faulty or inaccessible); M – special reading outside the billing cycle requested by the customer (e.g. after a move).

Consumption tiers (progressive tariff): household electricity – up to 125 kWh, 125–250 kWh, 250–1,000 kWh, above 1,000 kWh; household gas – up to 1,125 Th, 1,125–2,500 Th, 2,500–7,500 Th, above 7,500 Th. Non-household electricity – up to 250 kWh, 250–1,000 kWh, above 1,000 kWh; non-household gas – up to 2,500 Th, 2,500–7,500 Th, above 7,500 Th. Double tariff: code 52 – peak 17:00–21:00 at 811.47 cDA/kWh, off-peak 178.07 cDA/kWh; code 53 – night 22:30–06:00 at 120.50 cDA/kWh, day 06:00–22:30 at 486.98 cDA/kWh. Triple tariff (code 51): peak 17:00–21:00 at 811.47 cDA/kWh; full hours 06:00–17:00 and 21:00–22:30 at 216.45 cDA/kWh; night 22:30–06:00 at 120.50 cDA/kWh. Tariffs are the same nationwide.

Consumption formula: (new index − old index) × coefficient. Electricity billed in kWh, gas in thermies. Energy amount (HT) = sum over tiers of quantity × unit price.

Fixed charges (redevances): 4.37 DA per kW per month for electricity, and a flat 28.5 DA per month for gas. "Ces redevances sont facturées même lorsqu'il n'y a pas eu de consommation d'énergie."

Fees and services: charges for paid services such as installing or replacing a meter. Total HT = energy + fixed charges + fees.

VAT (TVA): 9% on household tiers 1 and 2, non-household tier 1 and all fixed charges; 19% on household tiers 3 and 4 and non-household tiers 2 and 3.

Broadcasting fee (redevance TV): 25 DA for consumption above 70 kWh up to 190 kWh; 50 DA for 190–390 kWh; 100 DA above 390 kWh.

Housing tax (taxe d'habitation): annual; 300 DA (residential) and 1,200 DA (professional) in all communes, or 600 DA and 2,400 DA in daïra capitals and in the communes of Algiers, Annaba, Constantine and Oran.

Energy contribution: energy benefits for Sonelgaz employees and retirees; State support for customers in southern wilayas – 65% off for household low-voltage customers and farmers up to 12,000 kWh/year, 25% off for non-agricultural economic activities up to 200,000 kWh/year; three high-plateau wilayas (Djelfa, El Bayadh, Naâma): 10% off for low- and medium-voltage customers.

REPE/RGPE: instalments for connection costs (REPE electricity, RGPE gas).

Net amount TTC = HT + VAT + broadcasting fee + housing tax + energy contribution + REPE/RGPE. Stamp duty (droit de timbre): calculated on the TTC total and payable only when paying in cash. Total to pay = net TTC + stamp duty.

Payment due date: after this date, the distributor may suspend supply if payment has not been made. Previous unpaid invoices are shown. EBP and EBB keys are check digits to avoid input errors when paying at Algérie Poste (EBP) or banks (EBB).

Information section: average daily cost = total ÷ 90 days; CREG operating contribution (included in tariff, shown for transparency); consumption chart over the last four billing cycles; payment options: commercial agencies, Algérie Poste, banks and online payment.

title: CREG – Demander une information (FAQ consommateurs)
text:
CREG – Consumer FAQ on electricity and gas.

Connections (raccordement):
- The distributor normally carries out connection works, from receipt of the request until commissioning. Alternatively, the applicant can use a company approved by the distributor under a supervision contract.
- A simple connection (branchement simple) applies if the property is within 25 m of the electricity network or 20 m of the gas network. Beyond that, a network extension is needed.
- Applicants submit a request with a copy of ID and proof of occupancy of the premises. A technical study is followed by a quote (devis), valid for two months. Works start after payment and the necessary administrative approvals.
- For gas, the meter is installed only after satisfactory leak tests and a conformity certificate from the installer.
- Simple connections take up to 10 days. Extension timelines are given in the quote.

Power and flow: electricity power is reserved by the distributor based on your needs, in kW. Low-voltage customers choose from values set by CREG decision D/11-13/CD (26 September 2013). Maximum gas flow for low-pressure customers is set by CREG decision D/04-13/CD (26 September 2013).

Meter reading: meters are read quarterly for low-voltage and low-pressure customers, and monthly for commercial and industrial customers. The meter number is the last four digits shown on the device.

Bills and payment: bills include a fixed fee (metering, billing, reading), charges for the power made available, energy consumption and State taxes. Payment options: cash or cheque at a commercial agency or post office; bank or postal account transfer; direct debit; or online via Edahabia, CIB or the WIMPAY-BNA app. Low-voltage and low-pressure bills are due within 15 days, after which supply may be cut without notice. Commercial and industrial bills are due within one month, after which formal notice is given before cutting supply. Reconnection requires payment of arrears plus cut-off and reconnection fees.

Where to get help: your supplier's commercial agency or Sonelgaz Distribution (SADEG); consumer protection associations (list on the Ministry of Commerce website); CREG.

Filing a complaint with CREG: possible if you are dissatisfied with how your request was handled, or if the distributor has not responded within three months. Submit by hand at CREG headquarters (Sunday to Thursday, 9:00–16:00), by post, by fax, by email to recours@creg.gov.dz, or through the online form. Acknowledgment of receipt within 3 days; processing time depends on the complaint's nature and complexity.

title: CREG – State Support (Soutien de l'État)
text:
CREG – State support for electricity consumers in the South and High Plateaus.

Purpose: under the State's policy of supporting populations in the South, electricity consumption reductions apply to low- and medium-voltage customers in 13 wilayas.

Covered wilayas – South (10): Adrar, Laghouat, Biskra, Béchar, Tamanrasset, Ouargla, Illizi, Tindouf, El Oued and Ghardaïa. High Plateaus (3): Djelfa, El Bayadh and Naâma.

Support levels:
1. Household subscribers and farmers (low and medium voltage): reduced rate on consumption up to 12,000 kWh per year; consumption above that is billed at the regular price. Legal basis: Article 137 of Law No. 16-14 (Finance Law for 2017).
2. Non-agricultural economic subscribers (low and medium voltage): reduced rate on consumption up to 200,000 kWh per year; consumption above that is billed at the regular price. Same legal basis.
3. High Plateaus subscribers (low and medium voltage): Interministerial Instruction No. 02 of 7 August 2001 on reducing electricity billing.

(The percentages on this page are displayed as '0%' – a display issue. CREG's 'Comment lire votre facture' page states 65% for household low-voltage customers and farmers in the South up to 12,000 kWh/year, 25% for non-agricultural economic activities up to 200,000 kWh/year, and 10% for low- and medium-voltage customers in Djelfa, El Bayadh and Naâma.)

Contact CREG: contact@creg.gov.dz, +213 28 91 03 01.

title: CREG – Dangers of Gas Leaks
text:
CREG – Dangers of gas leaks (advice and safety).

Improper use of natural gas can cause serious accidents. A gas leak can cause explosions and fires.

Properties of natural gas: it is invisible; it is asphyxiating; it is explosive; it is odorised, so a leak can be detected by smell.

If you smell gas, do not: create a flame or spark; smoke; use any phone at home, landline or mobile; light a match; use the doorbell (knock on the door instead); turn on light switches.

What to do in case of a leak:
1. Close the main gas valve.
2. Open doors and windows to ventilate the home.
3. Evacuate the premises immediately.
4. Call emergency services from outside.

Safety tips: keep the main gas valve accessible; replace the cooker's connection hoses at the end of their recommended usage period; close the main valve when gas will not be used for long periods; have the installation checked regularly by a professional and make sure the pipes are sealed.

Other CREG safety topics: electricity hazards; dangers of carbon monoxide (CO). Contact CREG: +213 28 91 03 01 / 02, contact@creg.gov.dz. Sonelgaz distribution call centre: 33 03.

title: SNTF – Services en gares
text:
SNTF – Services in stations.

Opening hours: stations serve passengers every day of the week, including public holidays. Some close overnight, between the last arriving train and the first departing one.

Staff assistance: station personnel help travellers prepare their trips, with information, bookings (réservations), ticket sales and complaints (réclamations).

Accessibility: current stations offer easy access to the waiting hall and platforms for people with reduced mobility (PMR).

Prayer facilities: most stations have prayer rooms and a restroom set up for ablutions.

Refreshments: most stations have snack bars, and some long-distance and regional trains have dining cars (Restau RAIL).

Free on-board amenities: comfort and sleeper trains offer tea, mineral water, newspapers, breakfast and wipes, depending on class.

SNTF network (from homepage): about 4,498 km of track covering 30 wilayas; more than a hundred passenger stations; train types: suburban (banlieue), regional, long-distance (grandes lignes) and freight. Contact: 21-23 Boulevard Mohamed V, Alger; (213) 21 71 15 10; contact@sntf.dz.

title: SNTF – À bord du train
text:
SNTF – On-board services.

Comfort: SNTF is modernising its fleet to international standards. Air conditioning is provided on long-distance and regional trains, and newer units serve the Algiers suburban lines. The new long-distance Coradia train is bi-mode diesel/electric (25 kV), up to 160 km/h, 6 cars, 254 seats including 60 in first class, with accessibility for persons with reduced mobility.

Information systems: suburban and intercity trains have audio-visual displays showing stations, destinations, time and outside temperature.

Staff: reception and assistance agents from the subsidiary SNTF Rail-Services provide travel information, help passengers and oversee safety and comfort. About 222 ticket inspectors (contrôleurs) and 375 train chiefs (chefs de train) work across the network; inspectors check tickets, train chiefs handle pre-departure safety checks and passenger safety.

Restrooms: long-distance units have accessible restrooms for elderly passengers, pregnant women and people with disabilities.

Cleaning: electric units are cleaned daily at a dedicated facility (with Stadler); diesel trains are cleaned before each departure.

Food and drink: kiosks at most stations, plus restaurant cars on long-distance routes, some items by trolley service. Complimentary items (tea, mineral water, newspapers, breakfast) on certain classes, wipes on sleeper and couchette trains.

Safety equipment: CO2 fire extinguishers, first-aid kits, stretchers, alarm signals.

Why take the train (homepage): group travel (54 seats per car), baggage tolerance, sleepers on long trips, buffet, service every day of the year, on-board toilets, fare reductions.

title: ARPCE – Portabilité des Numéros Mobiles
text:
ARPCE – Mobile number portability (Portabilité des Numéros Mobiles, PNM) project.

Legal definition: Law No. 18-04 of 10 May 2018 setting the general rules for post and electronic communications defines number portability as the "possibilité pour un abonné de conserver son numéro lorsqu'il change d'opérateur" (the possibility for a subscriber to keep their number when changing operator).

Purpose: portability is an effective way to increase competition in the electronic communications market.

Public consultation: on 29 July 2021, ARPCE launched a public consultation with the three mobile operators on the practical, technical, legal, organisational and pricing conditions for mobile number portability in Algeria.

Regulatory texts:
- Executive Decree No. 21-199 of 11 May 2021 setting the conditions and procedures for implementing mobile number portability.
- Decision No. 18/SP/PC/ARPCE/2021 of 27 June 2021 setting the practical implementation rules.
- Decision No. 37/SP/PC/ARPCE/2022 of 13 July 2022.
- Decision No. 55/SP/PC/ARPCE/2022 of 29 August 2022.

ARPCE lists PNM under its 'Grands Dossiers' (major files) section as a project.

title: IDOOM ADSL – Algérie Télécom
text:
Algérie Télécom – IDOOM ADSL (home internet for individuals).

Overview: Algérie Télécom offers unlimited internet through IDOOM ADSL packages, with speeds up to 20 Mbps ("Enjoy unlimited Internet access with IDOOM ADSL!"). Subscriptions can be made online or at a local store (agence commerciale).

Plans and prices (per month): 10 Mbps – 1,600 DZD; 15 Mbps – 1,999 DZD; 20 Mbps – 2,599 DZD. (A separate price list on the page shows monthly rates of 1,600, 2,000, 2,200 and 2,400 DZD without speed labels.) Plans of 15 Mbps and above include free access to Dzair Play, Algérie Télécom's video-on-demand service.

Higher speeds: ADSL cannot exceed 20 Mbps for technical reasons. Idoom VDSL offers 50 Mbps, and Idoom Fibre offers up to 1 Gbps.

Choosing a plan: consider the number of simultaneous users, main uses (downloads, streaming, data transfer) and line eligibility. An eligibility test checks your line's maximum speed; it requires your landline number.

Subscribing: apply online through the Online Request form or at a local store. Required documents: a copy of your ID, proof of address, and a completed, signed form. Every subscription carries a 12-month commitment, during which you cannot switch to a lower offer. The modem is not included and must be bought separately at points of sale.

Recharging and paying bills: online payment with Edahabia or CIB cards, or recharge cards and vouchers from stores or approved resellers. Other channels: indirect points of sale (kiosks, cybercafés, tobacco shops), the website and official app, BaridiMob, the WIMPAY-BNA app, and calling 1500 from a landline or mobile. Bills can be paid at a store, the post office, or through your Customer Space. If you cannot pay, Algérie Télécom offers a payment schedule (échéancier). If your phone bill is under 3,000 DZD, you can still recharge your internet subscription and reactivate it.

Business customers: IDOOM ADSL is for personal customers only; businesses can choose Idoom ADSL Pro, Idoom Fibre Pro or Moohtarif.

Support: social networks, a local store, or call 12 from a landline or mobile.

title: Customer Space – Algérie Télécom
text:
Algérie Télécom – Customer Space (Espace client).

The Customer Space is an online portal where subscribers manage their services. It covers Idoom Fixe (landline), Idoom ADSL, Idoom Fibre and Idoom 4G LTE; each customer on these plans can create a secure personal space.

Services available: manage your subscription; track your consumption; recharge your internet account; learn about online e-payment; view, download and pay your landline (fixe) bills; check subscription expiry dates; follow recharge operations; view your personal information.

How to access it:
1. Go to the account section and open the menu.
2. Click 'Customer space'.
3. Log in according to your subscription type: Idoom Fixe, ADSL or Fibre, or Idoom 4G LTE.
4. Follow the steps on screen.

Forgotten password: in the Customer space, click 'Forget password?'; a renewal email will be sent to your email address.

Assistance: contact your nearest store (agence commerciale), or call 12 from a landline or mobile phone to reach a call-centre advisor. Internet can also be recharged by calling 1500.

title: CREG – Making an Appeal
text:
CREG – Making an appeal (consumer recourse) – English version.

Purpose: under Article 115 of Law No. 02-01 of 5 February 2002, CREG protects consumers' rights regarding the supply, quality and continuity of electricity and gas service. It receives and processes complaints and appeals under its published procedures.

When to contact CREG – disputes with your distributor, such as: delayed or unprocessed requests for connection, modification or relocation of facilities; unaddressed outages, repairs or safety issues; billing disputes (excessive amounts, incorrect meter readings, cumulative consumption); requests to change the supply contract (tariff, power or flow rate); reconnection after disconnection for non-payment; voltage or pressure drops, metering issues, follow-up rights and compensation for incidents.

Before contacting CREG: submit your complaint first to the distributor (Sonelgaz – Distribution) under its internal complaint procedure approved by CREG. You may also consult a consumer protection association.

When to appeal: if you receive no response within a maximum of two months (the Arabic version of the page states three months), or the response is unsatisfactory. Include supporting documents, such as copies of your letters to the distributor and any replies.

How to submit: online via the Iltimess platform (iltimess.creg.dz) or the online form; in person at CREG headquarters, Sunday to Thursday, 9:00 to 16:00; by mail to CREG, Section N°04 lot n°788 Zone d'activité Amara, Cheraga, Algiers; by fax 028 91 03 02; by email recours@creg.gov.dz.

What happens next:
1. CREG checks admissibility and competence within five working days (the Arabic version states three working days) and notifies you.
2. If outside CREG's competence, you receive a letter saying so.
3. An appeal may be inadmissible if you did not first approach the distributor, your file is incomplete, or a court is examining or has resolved the dispute.
4. If admissible, CREG asks the distributor for explanations and gives it up to 15 days to respond.
5. If the distributor's position is valid, CREG closes the case and explains why.
6. If unfounded, CREG asks it to comply; if it does not, CREG rules in the complainant's favour.
7. CREG may convene the parties to seek an amicable solution.
8. Either party may take the dispute to the competent courts.

Contact: +213 28 91 03 01; +213 28 91 03 02; contact@creg.gov.dz.

title: COSOB – L'ouverture d'un compte titres
text:
COSOB (Commission d'Organisation et de Surveillance des Opérations de Bourse) – Guide: opening a securities account (compte titres).

1. Open a cash account: securities (shares, bonds, SICAV shares, FCP units, Treasury securities and financial products) must be bought or sold through a "teneur de compte-conservateur habilité par la COSOB" (custodian account-keeper approved by COSOB). You open a cash account there: a current account for individuals or a business account for legal entities.

2. Open a securities account: it records your trades and all events affecting your holdings (subscriptions, allocations, coupons, redemptions). Individuals: before opening, the custodian verifies your identity, your address, and that you have the legal capacity and status needed. Legal entities: the custodian verifies that the representative holds valid authority. Documents: you complete an account opening form and sign an account agreement ("convention de compte") in two copies; you keep one copy. The cash and securities accounts operate together: buying securities credits your securities account and debits your cash account; selling does the reverse.

3. Place orders: a signed buy or sell order is submitted to your custodian with all information needed for proper execution; it also authorises the corresponding movements in your cash and securities accounts.

4. Monitor your transactions: the custodian must provide an execution notice (avis d'opéré) confirming your order was carried out, and a periodic account statement showing your holdings in quantities and values.

Minimum contents of the account agreement: identity of the signatories (and how authorised persons are identified and informed); services covered and categories of securities; the custodian's fees; the agreement's duration; the custodian's confidentiality obligations; characteristics of orders, how they are sent and how the client is informed of execution; how the client receives information on movements, account statements and other regulatory information.

title: COSOB – Investir en bourse
text:
COSOB – Guide: Investing on the stock exchange (Investir en bourse).

The stock exchange: the Algiers exchange (Bourse d'Alger) is a regulated market where companies raise capital and investors place savings. Created by Legislative Decree No. 93-10 of 23 May 1993, as amended. Three bodies: COSOB (market regulator), SGBV (Société de Gestion de la Bourse des Valeurs, manages the Bourse d'Alger), and Algérie Clearing (central depository, settlement and clearing).

Products traded: shares (actions) – rights to information, voting at general meetings, dividends, preferential subscription, liquidation proceeds and bonus shares; dividends are set by the general meeting and not guaranteed. Bonds (obligations) – the investor lends to the issuer, which pays interest at a rate fixed at issuance and repays principal at maturity; types include corporate bonds and State bonds (OAT) with maturities of 7, 10 and 15 years. Other securities: investment certificates, voting-right certificates, participating securities, convertible bonds, bonds with subscription warrants.

Advantages and risks: possible capital gains and tax exemptions on income and gains; risks include capital losses, limited market liquidity, company bankruptcy (shares) and counterparty risk (bonds).

Buying and selling: individuals cannot trade directly; they must go through an approved Intermediary in Stock Market Operations (IOB); State bonds also involve Treasury Specialists (SVT). Primary market subscriptions are handled by banks and IOBs. Investors must open a securities account linked to a cash account, with a valid ID, a completed account opening form and a signed account agreement in two copies.

Orders: an order is an instruction to the IOB stating direction (buy/sell), the security, quantity, any price limit, validity period and the investor's details. The IOB checks that the investor has the securities or funds. Types: limit orders; market orders; day orders (one session); open-ended orders (until end of the current calendar month); time-limited orders (up to 30 days); good-till-executed orders (up to three calendar weeks); all-or-nothing orders (temporarily suspended); unconditional orders (partial execution allowed).

Execution: shares and corporate bonds trade on Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday; State bonds (OAT) trade Sunday through Thursday. Trades are executed electronically by fixing (one price per security per session). Block trades at the end of each session. Settlement at J+3 for securities and J+1 for OATs through Algérie Clearing. Securities are dematerialised and held in securities accounts by account keepers.

title: Air Algérie – Réclamation (Claims)
text:
Air Algérie (state carrier) – Claims procedure.

1. Flight delays, cancellations, denied boarding, staff behaviour or services: submit the claim through the online complaints platform https://doleances.airalgerie.dz/.

2. Baggage incidents (missing or damaged bags): before leaving the airport, report the problem at the airport baggage complaints service (Litige bagages). You will receive a Property Irregularity Report (PIR) with a file number; keep it. If you get no response, you can resend the request by post to the nearest Air Algérie representation. Include: personal details (full name, address, email, phone number); travel details (travel date, ticket number, flight number, itinerary); supporting documents (copy of the PIR, copies of your ticket and those of anyone who travelled with you, boarding pass, baggage tag, and excess baggage ticket if applicable). Liability limits for mishandled baggage are set out in the General Conditions of Carriage.

3. Problems with online purchases (booking or payment) made by international credit card, Algérie Poste EDAHABIA or CIB card: submit the claim through the complaints platform and select the payment method used.

4. AIR ALGERIE PLUS loyalty programme (miles, card delivery, login/password, card benefits): submit through the complaints platform with full name, email, phone number, membership number, travel date and ticket number.

Contact Center: Algeria +213 21 98 63 63; short code (Algeria) 3302; France +33 1 76 54 40 00; Spain +34 9 12 69 34 34 / +34 9 19 45 82 02; United Kingdom +44 2045 253188; Saudi Arabia +966 12 225 2160.

title: Air Algérie – Lost and damaged baggage
text:
Air Algérie – Lost, delayed and damaged baggage.

Lost baggage: before leaving the arrival airport, contact Air Algérie's baggage service and present the baggage receipt (tag) issued at check-in. If the reported bag is not found within 2 days, send a complete list of its contents (one list per bag) and all required baggage identification tags.

Missing items from baggage: provide the airport service in charge with all required documents and complete the appropriate form to help the search. Declare missing items within 3 days after the flight.

Valuables: Air Algérie disclaims responsibility for loss or damage to valuables transported without prior declaration.

Compensation and liability limits are set out in the General Conditions of Carriage (Conditions Générales de Transport). Claims can also be filed via https://doleances.airalgerie.dz/ (see Air Algérie claims page). Contact center Algeria: +213 21 98 63 63, short code 3302.

title: Air Algérie – Piece Concept (franchise bagages)
text:
Air Algérie – Free baggage allowance (Piece Concept).

Air Algérie offers a free checked baggage allowance on all flights. The allowance depends on the route, the cabin class (Economy, Business or First) and the passenger's loyalty card status at check-in. Confirm your allowance at booking or on your e-ticket.

Reading your e-ticket: "1Pc" = one checked bag up to 23 kg, plus one free cabin bag. "2Pc" = two checked bags up to 23 kg each, plus one free cabin bag.

Checked bag limits: maximum size 158 cm (length + width + depth); maximum weight 23 kg.

Children (2–11): same allowance as adults. Infants (under 2): one checked bag of up to 10 kg; a parent or guardian can also check one stroller or car seat free of charge.

Reduced mobility: passengers can check a fully foldable wheelchair, plus splints or crutches.

Excess baggage: bags over 23 kg and up to 32 kg are charged according to a published tariff. Bags over 32 kg are not accepted at check-in and must be shipped as cargo. Oversized bags over 158 cm but no more than 203 cm can be checked if they fit in the hold, for a flat fee of 12,000 DZD / 80 euros. Excess fees vary by route (tariff PDFs on the site).

Air Algérie Plus extra bags: Djurdjura – no extra baggage benefit; Chélia – one extra piece on all destinations except domestic flights, DXB, IST and connecting flights via Algiers (6th freedom); Tahat – one extra piece on all international and domestic destinations. Bag premium: reduced miles rate (500 miles less), one per flight per passenger.

Conditions: extra baggage is subject to availability, may be limited for security reasons, cannot be transferred to another passenger or flight, and cannot be bought for infants under 2.

title: Air Algérie – Allowance and excess bag
text:
Air Algérie – Additional and excess baggage.

Additional baggage: if your bags exceed the allowed number or size, or you want to bring extra bags, you can add pieces on top of your free allowance. Rates are published in a separate PDF ('Tarifs').

International excess: a bag counts as excess when it is over 158 cm (length + width + depth) and over 23 kg.

Overweight bags: bags over 23 kg and up to 32 kg are charged at the published rates. Bags over 32 kg are not accepted at check-in and must be sent as cargo (fret).

Oversize bags: bags over 158 cm but not over 203 cm can be checked if they fit in the aircraft hold, for a flat fee of 12,000 DZD (about €80).

Free allowance: see the Piece Concept page (1Pc / 2Pc of 23 kg each depending on route, class and loyalty status).

title: ARPCE – Service Universel des Communications Électroniques
text:
ARPCE – Universal Service of electronic communications (Service Universel des Télécommunications, SUT). Page dated 11 October 2020.

Purpose: to give every resident, regardless of location or social status, access to basic telecom services, especially internet access, at affordable prices. It is a public policy and land-planning tool promoting social cohesion by reducing disparities. Market forces alone cannot guarantee reasonable prices in remote areas operators find unprofitable to serve.

Funding: licensed operators and authorisation holders pay an annual contribution of 3% based on annual turnover. The State can also contribute, with amounts set by the finance law.

Legal evolution:
- Law 2000-03 (2000): established universal service as a founding principle for opening the postal and telecom markets to competition.
- Executive Decree 03-232 (2003): objectives including network access, continuity, reasonable pricing and specified quality of service.
- Executive Decree 17-106 (2017): raised the minimum speed from 512 kbit/s to 1 Mbit/s and required public education institutions to be connected at at least 1 Mbit/s.
- Law 18-04 (2018): created a multisector commission chaired by the minister to develop and manage the SUT and a support fund.
- Executive Decree 18-246 (2018): objectives including emergency call routing, telephone service, fixed and mobile internet in uncovered areas at a minimum of 2 Mbit/s, interconnection of public education and health institutions, basic infrastructure, and support for ORSEC emergency plans.
- Executive Decree 18-247 (2018): rules for managing the support fund; ARPCE and the ministry carry out ex-post checks on operators' compliance.

title: ARPCE – Service Universel de la Poste
text:
ARPCE – Universal postal service (Service Universel de la Poste). Last updated 21 January 2021.

Legal framework: Law No. 18-04 of 10 May 2018 defines the universal postal service as a minimum offer of basic postal and financial services, of specified quality, available nationwide on a permanent basis at affordable rates. Executive Decree No. 18-246 of 9 October 2018 sets its content, the applicable tariffs and how it is financed.

Content of the universal postal service:
- Letter mail up to 2 kg, including books, catalogues and periodicals.
- Registered mail (envois recommandés) and items with declared value.
- Parcels (colis postaux) up to 20 kg.
- Telegrams.
- Mail for the visually impaired (cécogrammes).
- Payment of pensions and social benefits.
- Regular collection and delivery, including in sparsely populated or hard-to-reach areas.
- Dedicated counters for people with specific needs.
- Postal presence in all urban areas.

Objectives: sustaining postal activity, universal access, continuity of the public postal service, affordable access to quality postal and financial services, better administrative, financial and service-quality performance, and security of deposited funds.

Financing: possible State funding set in the finance law; contributions from postal operators – 3% of pre-tax turnover for operators other than the universal service operator, and 3% of annual gross accounting profit for operators under the simple declaration regime.

Related texts: Law No. 18-04; Executive Decree No. 18-247 on managing the universal postal and electronic communications support fund. The universal service operator is Algérie Poste.

title: SNTF – Trains de banlieues
text:
SNTF – Suburban trains (trains de banlieue). Page dated 18 February 2018.

Rolling stock: FLIRT electric units designed and built by Stadler Rail (Switzerland), up to 160 km/h, articulated with two to six cars, can be coupled in multiple units. In 2006 SNTF ordered 64 units for the Algiers suburban network; the first was delivered in 2010.

Algiers ridership: 32.6 million passengers a year, about 91,000 a day, about 900 per train.

Algiers suburban network: 26 stations served by electric units on three axes:
- Alger – El Harrach: Alger, Agha, Ateliers, Hussein Dey, Caroubier, El Harrach.
- West: Gué de Constantine to El Affroun, including Blida and Boufarik.
- East: Oued Smar to Thénia, including Bab Ezzouar and Boumerdès.
Distances: 54 km from Alger to Thénia; 68 km from Alger to El Affroun.

Other cities: Constantine suburban network has 12 stations, Annaba 6 and Oran 9, with diesel services covering 50 km from Constantine, 15 km from Annaba and 38 km from Oran.

Fares: weekly and monthly suburban subscriptions (Annaba, Constantine, Oran) give 30% and 40% off; the Carte Verte for Algiers suburban lines gives 30% off weekly and 40% off monthly, quarterly, semi-annual and annual (see SNTF 'Avantages tarifaires'). The page gives no timetables; use the train search on www.sntf.dz.

Safety: "LE RESPECT DU CODE DE LA ROUTE ET DE LA SIGNALISATION EST VITAL" at unguarded level crossings.

title: SNTF – Trains de grandes lignes
text:
SNTF – Long-distance trains (grandes lignes). Page dated 18 February 2018.

Fleet: trains pulled by GM-EMD diesel-electric locomotives with DEV INOX coaches.

Service: SNTF offers 12 long-distance trains daily:
- Algiers – Oran (round trip): 8 trains, 4 of them comfort class.
- Algiers – Constantine (round trip): 2 trains.
- Algiers – Annaba (round trip): 2 trains, with 1st- and 2nd-class couchettes and seated coaches.

Refurbishment: coaches are being rehabilitated at the Sidi Bel Abbès rail maintenance workshops by an Algerian workforce; refurbished coaches get air conditioning, a passenger information system, power outlets and USB ports.

New trains: in 2015 SNTF ordered 17 'Coradia Polyvalent' trains from Alstom (bi-mode diesel/electric, up to 160 km/h, 254 seats including 60 first class, PMR accessible) to serve Algiers, Constantine, Oran, Annaba and Béchar among others.

Fares: round-trip tickets over 400 km get 20% off and are valid 2 months; youth (15–28) and senior cards give 20% off on journeys over 100 km; large-family card 30% off in 2nd class (see SNTF 'Avantages tarifaires').

title: SNTF – Trains régionaux
text:
SNTF – Regional trains. Page dated 18 February 2018.

CAF ZZ 22 railcars: units can be coupled up to three at a time (nine cars); designed for regional traffic with air conditioning and a passenger information system; four 338 kW motors, top speed 160 km/h. Milestones: first unit received in Algiers 28 Nov 2007; Algiers–Blida in 28 minutes (30 Jan 2008); Algerian speed record of 177 km/h between Chlef and Oran (3 Feb 2008); service launched between Algiers and Sétif (about 300 km) in 3h33 on 10 Mar 2008.

Daily regional services – railcars (autorails):
- Algiers region (4 units): Alger–Béjaïa, Alger–Sétif, Alger–Chlef, Alger–M'Sila–Batna.
- Oran region (2 units): Oran–Chlef, Oran–Maghnia.
- Constantine region (2 units): Constantine–Biskra.

Diesel regional trains:
- Algiers: Chlef–Khemis, Alger–Bouira, Beni Mansour–Bouira, Bordj Bou Arréridj–M'Sila.
- Constantine: Touggourt–Biskra, Batna–Aïn Touta.
- Oran: Oran–Tlemcen, Oran–Sidi Bel Abbès, Tlemcen–Ghazaouet, Oran–Relizane, Oran–Aïn Témouchent.
- Annaba: Annaba–Tébessa, Annaba–Chihani, Souk Ahras–Sidi Hmissi.

Fares: ordinary regional subscription 35% off (2nd class, up to 200 km); carnet of coupons on railcars up to 47% off (homepage).

title: COSOB – Alertes (mises en garde)
text:
COSOB – Investor alerts (mises en garde). Titles and subjects of the warnings published (full texts in linked PDFs/images):

1. "Mise en garde contre l'exercice non autorisé d'activités réglementées" (September 2026): warning about the unauthorised performance of regulated stock-market activities.
2. "Mise en garde contre les appels de souscription de valeurs mobilières" (May 2024): warning about solicitations to subscribe to securities and other financial products through public savings appeals (appel public à l'épargne) not authorised by COSOB.
3. "Mise en garde contre les appels de souscription de valeurs mobilières proposés par des personnes" (May 2024): warning about subscription offers from persons who sell securities through public savings appeals or carry out regulated activities without authorisation.
4. "Mise en garde contre la publication de déclarations et commentaires attentatoires" (August 2024): warning that statements and comments damaging to listed companies may undermine market integrity and proper functioning.
5. "Mise en garde contre les offres proposant l'achat des actions" (August 2024): warning about offers to buy shares of companies listed on the Bourse d'Alger outside the regulatory framework of stock exchange trading.

Practical point (from COSOB guides): individuals may only trade listed securities through an approved IOB (Intermédiaire en Opérations de Bourse). Contact COSOB: communication@cosob.dz, +213 23 47 27 93.
